## Cycle 13: Admin-fee exclusions + dollar cap dropped by the Worker engine (shipped)

**Finding (HIGH, pure tenant overcharge).** The production TypeScript reconciliation
engine computed the administrative fee as a bare `share_after_cap × rate` and silently
discarded **three** persisted lease terms that constrain that fee. Each dropped term is a
pure overcharge billed to the tenant:

  - `admin_fee_cap`: a hard dollar ceiling on the computed fee.
  - `admin_fee_excludes_tax_insurance`: removes the default tax/insurance pool NAMES from
    the fee base.
  - `admin_fee_excluded_pools`: explicit pool NAMES removed from the fee base.

The Python oracle (`tenant_share.py:621-689`, `pool_allocation.py:140-223`) already honors
all three. The lease governs the fee, so the **Worker was the buggy party**. This is not a
divergence-toward-correctness call; the oracle is right and the Worker was under-charging
the lease's constraints into the tenant's bill.

**Fix.** `parseLeaseTerms` now reads the three keys from the recovery-profile JSONB (no
migration, the column is free-form), defaulting to `null` / `false` / `[]`, so any lease
**without** these terms is byte-identical to prior behavior. `computeAdminFee` shrinks the
fee **base** by an inclusion **ratio** (`included_pool / total_pool` over the grossed-up,
pre-management-cap pool breakdown) applied to the post-cap share, then applies the cap as a
`min()`. `resolveAdminFeeExcludedPools` resolves the exclusion set **once** (explicit list
wins; else the default T&I names when the flag is set) and the **same** set drives both the
aggregate fee base and the Layer-3 per-pool admin-fee attribution in
`allocatePoolBreakdowns`, so an excluded pool never receives a fee slice. Matching is by
exact lowercased pool NAME, mirroring the oracle's dict-key membership test.

**Money stays integer-cents.** `admin_base = roundDivide(shareAfterCap_cents ×
included_cents / total_cents)` is exact-rational half-up; `roundDivide` is now exported from
`money.ts` for this path. This is a **deliberate, penny-tighter divergence** from the
oracle, which derives the ratio via a Python float division (`Decimal(str(included/total))`)
then double-rounds; in ~1e-5 of exclusion cases the oracle lands 1 cent low and the
integer-rational result here is the correct party (CLAUDE.md: oracle parity is not
automatically correctness). Documented inline.

**Verification.** New `reconciliation-admin-fee-exclusion-cap.test.ts` (8 cases,
**RED-proven 5/8 fail** without the fix): positive control (full share × rate); cap binds;
cap above fee is a no-op; default-T&I exclusion by name; exact-name contract (a "Property
Taxes" pool is NOT caught by the default flag); explicit list by name; explicit list wins
over the flag; ratio-then-cap composition. Each asserts **both** the aggregate
fee/total **and** the per-pool Layer-3 attribution. Full suite **1752 passed / 12 skipped,
0 failed**; tsc 0, eslint 0.

**Code review** (two-stage opus): **SHIP**: no CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM. Confirmed
integer-cents purity, regression safety (empty set + null cap ⇒ prior behavior), RED-proven
tests, and that matching the oracle is financially correct CAM truth. One LOW (doc comment
overclaimed exact parity, **fixed**) and one NIT (sub-cent cap pre-rounding, acceptable,
only on mis-stored data).

**Ship.** branch `fix/c13-admin-fee-exclusion-cap` (commit `017328ac`) → merged `--no-ff`
to master `091af3d1`, pushed. Deployed `capveri-api` → **100%** on version
`3b28c92e-b3b5-47ef-896a-fc0de0ea8af7`; `GET /health` = healthy.

**Deferred (carried forward):** Finder D negative-base-unguarded-in-Worker (MEDIUM guard);
Finder B admin-fee rate >100%/negative guard (LOW, both engines); Finder A base-year
snapshot double-count (needs empirical confirmation whether base-year periods finalize into
snapshots); gross-up asymmetry (base not grossed up, needs `base_year_occupancy` schema
field + product decision); oracle `gross_up_target` hardcodes 0.95; unmatched-GL DB-column

## Cycle 14: Reject re-calculating a reconciliation over an already-FINALIZED period (data-integrity / cumulative-cap inflation)

**Found via** fresh parallel high-risk hunt over the reconciliation idempotency / lifecycle
surface (job → draft → finalize) rather than the calc engine. Four deep finders
(negative-clamp, fee-bounds, true-up sign convention, multi-period carry) returned CLEAN of
shippable money bugs (strong convergence) and rejected Finder 3's "opposite sign
convention" (the actual-billed module is internally consistent: `total_underbill_exposure` /
`total_overbill_exposure`, landlord lens; the comparison module is tenant-overcharge lens
with explicit `direction`). The real defect was in the WORKFLOW guard, not the math.

**The bug.** The reconciliation idempotency guard only checked **DRAFT** snapshots
(`countDraftSnapshots` / `deleteDraftSnapshots`), never finalized. Re-running calculate over
an already-**FINALIZED** (property, period) passed the guard (draftCount = 0), created fresh
drafts, and those drafts could be finalized into a **SECOND finalized snapshot** for the
same (lease, period). No DB unique constraint, no route guard, no finalized check anywhere.

**Impact (adversarial-verifier confirmed, worked number).** The duplicate double-counts in
the cumulative-cap prior-amounts history query (`reconciliation.ts` ~991): it `json_agg`s
`tenant_share_after_cap` over `status='finalized'` rows with `period_start_date < currentStart`,
and `priorAmounts.length` drives `yearsSinceBase = priorAmounts.length + 1` **plus** the bank
base. 2023 finalized twice at $105k each ⇒ 2024 `effectiveMax` $110,000 → **$120,000**
(+$10,000), and the inflation **compounds** every subsequent year. The oracle's year-dedup
branch (`data_fetcher.py:158-164`) is **disabled in prod** (`base_year=None`), so BOTH engines
shared this latent exposure, fixed Worker-side per divergence-toward-correctness.

**Why REJECT (not supersede).** Finalized snapshots are **immutable audit records** (warranty
certs `one_certificate_per_snapshot`, `trace_checksum`, `finalized_at/by`); `finalizeSnapshotById`
only flips `draft→finalized` in place (never inserts), and there is **NO** user-facing
reopen/delete route. Finalization is whole-period batch (`finalizeBatch` finalizes all drafts
for the period), so there is no legitimate "finalize lease A then recalc to add lease B" flow
that rejection breaks. The two snapshot-insert paths are `insertCalculationSnapshots` (drafts)
and that batch finalize, both now gated.

**The fix (two layers, neither bypassed by `force_recalculate`, force only deletes DRAFTS):**
- `createCalculationJob` checks `hasFinalizedSnapshotForPeriod` **inside the existing
  transaction**, before the job insert / draft-campaign upsert, and returns a new
  `period_finalized` state; the calculate route maps it to **HTTP 409**
  `period_already_finalized`.
- **Defense-in-depth:** the queue workflow `run()` re-checks `countFinalizedSnapshots > 0`
  and throws **before** `deleteDraftSnapshots` / insert, covering the race where a job is
  created while the period is still draft but runs after it is finalized.
- New repo methods `countFinalizedSnapshots` + helper `hasFinalizedSnapshotForPeriod` mirror
  `countDraftSnapshots` / `hasActiveLeaseForPeriod` byte-for-byte (status='finalized',
  `$3::date`/`$4::date` casts, property+org scoping, null-safe). New `period_finalized` arm
  added to the `CreateCalculationJobResult` union (exhaustive, type-safe).

**Verification.** RED-proven regression tests (all 3 fail without the fix, rest green):
repository returns `period_finalized` even with `force_recalculate=true` and inserts **no**
job/campaign (exactly 3 statements); route returns 409 `{ error: { code:
"period_already_finalized" } }`; workflow fails the job and deletes/inserts **nothing** when a
finalized snapshot exists, with **and** without `force_recalculate` (`deletedDrafts===false`,
`insertedSnapshots===[]`). Existing `creates calculation jobs…` repo test re-sequenced for the
new in-transaction query. Full suite **1755 passed / 23 skipped, 0 failed**; tsc 0, eslint 0.

**Code review** (independent opus, contrarian): **SHIP**: no BLOCKING. Confirmed root cause /
aggregation double-count, SQL predicate parity, guard placement closes reachability without
breaking first-time calc / force-over-drafts / multi-lease, defense-in-depth catches the
TOCTOU race, immutability of finalized, and error-shape serialization match. Only optional
style nits (extra round-trip; count-as-bool helper), left as prior-art-consistent.

**Ship.** branch `fix/c14-finalized-period-guard` (commit `eb06cc03`) → merged `--no-ff` to
master `f37e75d1`, pushed. Deployed `capveri-api` → **100%** on version
`ee536fc4-590c-4116-a537-29d9db11af8d`; `GET /health` = healthy.

**Deferred (chip / product decision, NOT autonomous):** manifestation 2, distinct
partial/overlapping sub-annual periods within one cap year (2023-H1 + 2023-H2) rolling into
the cumulative-cap year history is **under-specified CAM semantics**; reconcile with oracle
`caps.py` / `data_fetcher.py` year-dedup intent before any query-level dedup-by-year. Carried
forward from C13: Finder A base-year snapshot double-count empirical confirm; gross-up
asymmetry needing `base_year_occupancy` schema field; oracle `gross_up_target` hardcodes 0.95;
unmatched-GL DB-column persistence + suspense-pool routing.

## Cycle 15: partial multi-mapping GL split penny conservation (HIGH, shipped)

**Hunt.** Fresh 4-finder parallel sweep vs the Python oracle + CAM truth, each returning
reachability verdicts with worked examples: A = money/numeric DECODE precision in DB adapters;
B = RLS/org-scoping cross-tenant; C = penny-conservation in pool/lease allocation; D =
finalize/batch-finalize lifecycle races. Triage:
- **A: REJECTED.** porsager-cf registers parsers only for json/bool/date/bytea; bare `numeric`
  decodes to the raw text string (`connection.js:510`), never a JS float, and every money sink
  uses `Decimal`/`String`. No `double precision`/`float` columns exist in the schema. The
  `::text` casts are hygiene, not load-bearing for money precision. (The real decode hazard is
  date/timestamp → `Date`, already handled per `project_cf_postgres_date_decode`.)
- **B: REJECTED (one LOW note).** Cumulative-cap prior-amounts query is org-scoped; all target
  tables have RLS; every read carries `organization_id`. Worker DB layer uses service-role
  (bypasses RLS), so app-layer org predicates are the real defense, and they are present. LOW:
  four `loadCalculationDataset` sub-queries scope by `property_id` only, leaning on the
  create-time property→org binding; adding `and organization_id=$N` would harden a hypothetical
  property-reassignment TOCTOU (no exploit today). Held as future defense-in-depth.
- **D: REJECTED (LOW/MED, product calls).** Single + batch finalize and updateCell-vs-finalize
  are race-safe (single-tx `FOR UPDATE` + `status='draft'`-guarded `UPDATE … RETURNING`,
  0-rows→conflict, `finalized_requires_timestamp` CHECK + RLS draft-only policy). Warranty-cert
  path is unimplemented in the TS backend (moot). LOW: `finalizeBatch` flips the campaign row
  AFTER/OUTSIDE the snapshot tx (swallows failure → campaign can lag its finalized snapshots);
  single `finalizeSnapshot` never advances the campaign. MED (product policy): a manually
  overridden `total_recovery` survives later admin_fee/share edits, so a finalized snapshot can
  carry a total that doesn't tie to its parts. Flagged to owner, not shipped.
- **C: CONFIRMED HIGH, shipped this cycle (below).**

**Root cause (`aggregatePools`, `calculator.ts`).** A GL entry can match several pool mappings;
each books a slice (`entry × allocation`, half-up to integer cents). The prior code pinned the
final slice to the exact remainder ONLY when the entry was FULLY allocated (running `remaining`
hit 0). A legitimate **partial-recovery** config, two+ mappings on one account whose
allocations sum to < 100% (e.g. 0.50 + 0.30 = 80% recoverable, 20% unrecoverable), never drives
`remaining` to 0, so every slice was rounded independently:
`round(5c*0.50) + round(5c*0.30) = 3c + 2c = 5c` booked instead of the correct
`round(5c*0.80) = 4c`. A **same-signed** cent of operating expense manufactured per entry,
accumulating linearly (500 small entries → **$5.00** of phantom `total_operating_expenses`
flowing into gross-up, pro-rata, tenant recovery, over-billing the tenant). Shared with the
oracle's *intent* but the oracle (`pool_aggregator.aggregate_by_pools`) keeps exact Decimal per
pool and rounds once, so it conserves. **The Worker is the buggy party.**

**The fix (divergence-toward-correctness + oracle parity).** Restructure `aggregatePools` into
two phases per entry: (1) collect all matched `{poolTotal, allocation}` (same
`minRate(allocation, remaining)` 100% cap); (2) compute `target = round(entry × Σalloc)`
(`Σalloc = 1 − remaining`) and book each slice independently EXCEPT the **last** matched slice,
pinned to `target − Σ(prior)`. For a FULL split `Σalloc = 1` so `target = entry`, reproducing the
previous remainder-pin **byte-identically** (no regression on fully-allocated 3-way,
single-partial 60%, or misconfigured >100% sign-guard cases). Sign guard retained: if the pinned
last slice would flip the entry's sign, fall back to the plain rounded slice so a bad >100%
split can never manufacture an opposite-sign pool.

**Verification.** RED-proven: 2 new tests (single $0.05 / 0.50+0.30 → `$0.04` with per-pool
`3c`+`1c`; 4-entry accumulation → `$0.16` not `$0.20`) **fail before, pass after**. Full suite
**1757 passed / 23 skipped / 0 failed**; tsc 0; eslint 0.

**Code review** (independent opus, adversarial): **SHIP**: no BLOCKING. Confirmed the target is
oracle-faithful and the correct CAM direction (removes an over-bill), proved byte-identical
reproduction of the three previously-correct cases via worked numbers, found no case where
slices fail to sum to target / a pool flips sign / target is wrong, and cleared the
type/quality (no `any`/`as`/ignore). Non-blocking nits: `target` computed even when no pool
matched (harmless); `matched[i]!` repetition (applied, bound `const match` once); the Worker
still lacks the oracle's >100% validation rejection (separate latent gap, not this fix's).

**Ship.** branch `fix/c15-partial-split-penny-conservation` (commit `77eb5572`) → merged `--no-ff`
to master `c43bf6c9`, pushed. Deployed `capveri-api` → **100%** on version
`ebb3c72e-af59-434e-bced-75662a24cb7f`; `GET /health` = healthy.

## Cycle 17: GL parser drops parentheses+CR/DR combined amounts (shipped)

**Bug class:** silent expense vanishing (under-counts CAM costs, worst-direction failure
for a landlord). Reachable on the real production ingestion path.

**Finder sweep** over not-yet-exhausted high-risk areas. The pool-allocation >100% lead was
investigated and DISPROVED (oracle `validate_split_allocation` pool_aggregator.py:277-327 is
DEAD code never called in production; both sides apply the same runtime `min(remaining)` cap,
so entry $100 with 0.70+0.50=120% pool weights yields $100.00 total on BOTH sides, LOW,
non-shippable). A GL-parser finder claimed `($500.00)` was a TS-drop; independently DISPROVED
(the old `^\((.*)\)$` paren regex captures `$500.00` inside and the later `[$£€¥]` strip
removes the symbol → correctly -500.00). Narrowed the REAL bug to the **parens + CR/DR suffix
combination**.

**Defect:** `cloudflare-backend/src/domain/ingestion/csv-parser.ts` `cleanCurrency` detected
the leading paren only when `^\((.*)\)$` wrapped the WHOLE string. For `(1,234.56) CR` the
trailing ` CR` defeated that anchor, the CR-strip then left `(1,234.56)`, and the leftover
parens failed the `/^\d+(\.\d+)?$/` numeric gate → returned null → row dropped at
`normalizeRecord`. The oracle `backend/app/services/ingestion/cleaners.py`
`clean_currency_column` (13-62) imports **-1234.56** via its independent `is_cr_negative` mask.
So a genuine credit/expense line silently disappeared from the reconciliation.

**Fix:** replace fixed-order sign-stripping with INDEPENDENT mask detection (mirroring the
oracle's vectorized booleans): `parenNegative = startsWith("(") && endsWith(")")`,
`crNegative = endsWith("CR")`, `trailingNegative = endsWith("-")`, `leadingNegative` regex:
`negative = any`. Then strip decorations with parentheses removed FIRST so an interior CR/DR
(e.g. `(500 CR)`) becomes a strippable suffix. Parentheses now mark a negative whether or not
a CR/DR suffix follows. Money stays exact (Decimal ROUND_HALF_UP); the stricter numeric gate
still DROPS exotic forms (`1e3`/`+5`/`.5`) rather than inventing a value. DR remains positive.

**Verification:** 3 RED-proven regression tests added (`(1,234.56) CR` → -1234.56,
`(500 CR)` → -500.00, `($500.00)` → -500.00) plus the existing parity suites preserved. Full
gate: vitest **1761 passed / 23 skipped** (114 files), tsc 0, eslint 0. Opus adversarial
review = **NO ISSUES** (traced 19 edge inputs vs the oracle; bonus finding: the TS path is
*more* correct than the oracle on U+2212 unicode-minus, which the oracle sign-loses; all TS
divergences are in the SAFE direction, never invents or sign-flips a money value).

**Shipped:** branch fix/c17-gl-paren-cr-drop (54ab66a1) → merged --no-ff to master 517de082 →
pushed origin/master. Deployed capveri-api version `a7df587b-5496-454d-9738-fa7433461fb4`
(100%), `curl https://api.capveri.com/health` → `{"status":"healthy",...}`.

`normalize_base_year`/`should_normalize` schema gap (LOW); cap-bank engine-vs-ledger
before/after-cap split (needs lease-language input); `finalizeBatch` campaign-flip-outside-tx
(LOW); `total_recovery` manual-override decoupling at finalize (MED, product policy); C14

## Cycle 19: finalize total_recovery rounded HALF_EVEN, off the engine convention (shipped)

**Bug class:** billing-figure rounding parity break (1-cent under-billing on a sub-cent
manual override).

**Source:** Cycle 18 Finder B (queued, verified-real). Independently re-verified before shipping.

**Defect:** `cloudflare-backend/src/adapters/db/reconciliation.ts` `calculateDependentTotalRecovery`
recomputes a tenant's `total_recovery` (tenant_share_after_cap + admin_fee) when a landlord
manually overrides one of those cells via `PATCH /reconciliation/cells/:cellId` (unless
total_recovery itself is overridden). It rounded `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. The entire
calculation/billing layer rounds `ROUND_HALF_UP` (money.ts roundDivide, cumulative-cap.ts,
cap-bank-ledger.ts, occupancy in calculator.ts), and the engine that produces the NON-override
total_recovery sums exact integer cents via Money.add. The route schema `cellUpdateSchema`
validates with `/^\d+(\.\d+)?$/`, accepts ANY decimals, so a sub-cent override reaches this
sum and can land on a half-cent, where HALF_EVEN stored a total **1 cent below** the engine
convention (under-billing the landlord). HALF_EVEN was the lone outlier in the billing layer.

**Correctness basis:** no Python oracle exists for this TS-only manual-override feature, so
"correct" = consistent with the engine's own documented HALF_UP convention (CLAUDE.md: money is
Decimal.js ROUND_HALF_UP, toFixed(2)). The rent-roll parser's HALF_EVEN is a separate
ingestion/pandas-parity layer, confirmed unrelated, left untouched.

**Fix:** `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` → `ROUND_HALF_UP` (one constant) + explanatory comment.

**Verification:** confirmed via the route schema that sub-cent overrides are reachable (regex
allows any decimals); RED-proven test through the existing FakePostgresExecutor updateCell
harness (1000.00 + 0.125 override → 1000.125 → HALF_UP 1000.13, was 1000.12 under HALF_EVEN).
Full gate: vitest **1766 passed / 23 skipped** (114 files), tsc 0, eslint 0. Opus review =
**NO ISSUES** (confirmed change is exactly the rounding constant; HALF_UP is codebase-wide for
billing; every remaining HALF_EVEN is display/PDF formatting or ingestion parity, a different
layer; test distinguishes the modes and asserts the right param; direction removes a 1-cent
under-bill, correct for landlord-side billing).

**Shipped:** branch fix/c19-total-recovery-halfup (0db24752) → merged --no-ff to master
caa82298 → pushed origin/master. Deployed capveri-api version
`a70f4297-971e-4606-a33c-e30aeb932f29` (100%), health `{"status":"healthy",...}`.

## Cycle 20: bare GL "Description" header routed to memo, not account_description (shipped)

**Bug class:** GL field-semantics divergence: account name lands in the wrong
column, blank in audit/GL-narrative reports. Financial math unaffected.

**Source:** Cycle 18 Finder D BUG 2 (queued, verified-real). Re-verified vs oracle
before shipping.

**Defect:** `cloudflare-backend/src/domain/ingestion/csv-parser.ts` mapped a bare
`description`/`desc` GL header to the `description` memo field (yardiColumnMappings,
mriColumnMappings). In a GL export the bare "Description" column holds the GL ACCOUNT
name (e.g. "Landscaping"), so `account_description` came through blank and the account
name was hidden from audit/GL-narrative reports. The Python oracle
(yardi.py:333-334, mri.py:361-362) renames a bare description to `account_description`.

**Correctness basis (divergence-toward-correctness):** the oracle renames a bare
description to account_description BLINDLY, when a file has BOTH "Account Description"
AND "Description" columns, that collides (pandas duplicate-column rename) and the bare
column (a genuine per-line memo) is mishandled. So matching the oracle verbatim would
itself be wrong for the both-columns case. The correct rule: promote a bare-description
value to account_description ONLY when no explicit "Account Description" column
populated it; when both exist, the explicit one wins and the bare column stays a memo.

**Fix:** in `mapRecord`, after the header-mapping loop:
```ts
const memo = mapped.description ?? "";
if ((mapped.account_description ?? "").trim() === "" && memo.trim() !== "") {
  mapped.account_description = memo;
  delete mapped.description;
}
```
The promotion only fires when account_description is otherwise empty, never overwriting
a real mapped account name. `delete` nulls the memo downstream via emptyToNull(undefined).

**Verification:** RED-proven via the both-columns ingestion-routes test (which initially
failed when the first blanket-remap approach collided the columns, caught the edge case
and drove the guarded design). 4 new parser tests: Yardi/MRI bare Description → account_
description + memo null; bare Desc → account_description; and the negative branch (both
columns → explicit account_description wins, bare stays memo). Full gate: vitest
**1769 passed / 23 skipped** (114 files), tsc 0, eslint 0. Opus review = **APPROVE**
(guard is safe; generic-mapping behavior change is LOW/acceptable; delete nulls memo
correctly; no row-validity/amount/date impact; financial reasoning sound). Added the
reviewer's suggested negative-branch test before merge.

**Shipped:** branch fix/c20-gl-bare-desc-account-description (1df58264) → merged --no-ff
to master 706b6037 → pushed origin/master. Deployed capveri-api version
`3f69e8cd-39f1-4407-a51c-2eca6a7b084c` (100%), health `{"status":"healthy",...}`.

## Cycle 21: Admin-fee inclusion ratio uses post-management-cap pools (oracle parity)

**Defect (MEDIUM, confirmed real, divergence-FROM-correctness):** The administrative
fee base is `tenant_share_after_cap * inclusion_ratio` where `inclusion_ratio =
included_pools / total_pools` over `adminInclusionPools`. `calculateReconciliationSnapshots`
passed `grossedUpPools` (the PRE-management-fee-cap breakdown) as that basis
(calculator.ts:312, old). When a lease's `management_fee_percentage` cap binds (booked
fee > `rate * operating_base`), the non-recoverable fee excess remained in the ratio
denominator, understating the excluded share and **overcharging the tenant** on the admin
fee. The two trigger fields (`management_fee_percentage`, `admin_fee_excluded_pools` /
`admin_fee_excludes_tax_insurance`) are independent lease-profile fields and co-occur freely.

**Independent verification (rigor mandate, did NOT trust the finder):**
- Oracle uses the POST-cap breakdown. `_apply_management_fee_cap` reduces the mgmt-fee pool
  to the cap in BOTH `pool_breakdown` (tenant_share.py:359-360) AND `original_pool_breakdown`
  (362-367, comment: "so exclusion and admin-fee ratios use the recoverable amount").
  `exclusion_pool_breakdown = original_pool_breakdown` (post-cap, 456-458); the ratio
  denominator sums it at :645. So the oracle's admin ratio is genuinely post-cap.
- `leasePools` (calculator.ts:268, output of `capManagementFeePools(grossedUpPools, rate)`)
  differs from `grossedUpPools` ONLY in the mgmt-fee pool amount; when the cap does not bind
  the two are identical (every non-binding path returns the input unchanged) → common
  tax/insurance case provably unaffected.
- `adminInclusionPools` is consumed ONLY by `computeAdminFee` for the inclusion ratio
  (calculator.ts:933-940); never re-capped or double-counted. The recovery base uses the
  separate scalar `aggregateGrossedUp − managementFeeExcess`.
- Financially-correct basis = recoverable (post-cap) composition → oracle correct here, TS
  wrong. This is the OPPOSITE of a divergence-toward-correctness; matching the oracle IS the fix.

**Fix:** calculator.ts:319 `adminInclusionPools: grossedUpPools` → `leasePools` (post-cap);

## Cycle 22: Persisted source→target pool splits never applied by the Worker engine (HIGH, shipped)

**Finder claim (Finder C):** the production Worker reconciliation engine loads `pool_mappings`
but never loads or applies `pool_allocations` (the source→target pool SPLIT feature). A GL
entry's dollars stay entirely in the SOURCE pool, so any landlord who configured a split
(e.g. "route 40% of CAM-Shared to Parking", or "30% of an operating pool to a capital pool")
gets the WRONG recovery, the split silently does nothing in prod.

**Independent verification (both engines, worked example):**
- *Worker (pre-fix):* `aggregatePools` (calculator.ts) booked each matched slice with
  `match.poolTotal.amount = match.poolTotal.amount.add(slice)`, no source/target split path
  anywhere in the reconciliation domain. `pool_allocations` was never loaded by
  `loadCalculationDataset`. Confirmed by grep + full read.
- *Oracle (live, source of truth):* `backend/app/api/v1/reconciliation.py` loads
  pool_allocations and calls `aggregate_with_splits(entries, pool_mappings, split_allocations)`
  when non-empty, NOT dead code, it is the production Python path.
  `build_split_allocations_from_pool_allocations` (pool_aggregator.py:111-151) groups
  percentage rows by `source_pool_id` and emits one `SplitAllocation` per mapping on that
  source with `default_pool_id = mapping.pool_id` (the source). `aggregate_with_splits`
  persisted branch (502-591) routes `entry.amount * actual_allocation * pct` to each target
  per entry, remainder `(1 − Σpct)` to the source/default pool only when `Σpct < 1`.
- *Why it's real money, not relabeling:* a 40% split from an operating pool into a pool the
  lease EXCLUDES (capital) turns $400 of a $1000 entry non-recoverable → recovery $600 not
  $1000. Pinned by a regression test.

**Financial-correctness ruling:** the oracle is correct here and the Worker is wrong; this is
NOT a divergence-toward-correctness. Splits are an explicit landlord configuration with a
write-path validation (Σpct ≤ 100%); ignoring them mis-buckets recoverable cost across the
exclusion / management-cap / admin-fee boundaries the splits exist to redraw. Matching the
oracle structure IS the fix.

**Fix (port, byte-identical when no splits configured):**
- `calculator.ts`: new `CalculationPoolAllocationRecord` type + optional `poolAllocations`
  on `CalculationDataset`; `aggregatePools` builds `splitsBySource` (keyed by source pool id,
  equivalent to the oracle's (pool_id, pattern) keying since build_split emits one
  SplitAllocation per mapping with default=source) and fans each matched `slice` out across
  the source's targets. Penny conservation: book `round(slice·pct)` per target and PIN the
  final booking to `slice − Σprior` so parts re-sum to the slice exactly (last target pinned
  when Σpct==1; source remainder pinned when Σpct<1). Sign guard: pin only when it keeps the
  slice's sign, else fall back to the plain re-rounded share: a misconfigured >100% split
  cannot manufacture an opposite-sign pool. Empty allocations → original code path, byte-identical.
- `reconciliation.ts`: `loadCalculationPoolAllocations` (percentage rows only; org-scoped via
  `join expense_pools` + `exists(... properties.organization_id = $2)` for the raw-executor
  queue path that has no RLS session; `allocation_value::text` cast to dodge the porsager
  numeric-decode footgun; `order by created_at asc` for deterministic target order) wired into
  `loadCalculationDataset`'s Promise.all (now 7 sub-queries).

**Regression tests:** `reconciliation-pool-allocation-splits.test.ts` (5 tests, RED-proven by
temporarily forcing `poolAllocations` to `[]` at the call site → 3 split tests failed
`1000.00 != 600.00` / `0.00 != 500.01`, control passed): (1) partial 40% split CAM→Parking
($600/$400); (2) two-target 50/50 of $1000.01 penny-exact ($500.01/$500.00, source $0); (3)
40% split into an EXCLUDED capital pool drops recovery to $600.00 (real money); (4)
source-as-own-target (cam→cam 40% + cam→park 40% → CAM $600 / Parking $400); (5) no-allocations
control byte-identical. `reconciliation-repository.test.ts` RLS defense-in-depth test updated
for the 7th sub-query (asserts pool_allocations is org-scoped, param-index shift).

**Gate:** tsc 0, eslint 0, vitest **1777 passed / 0 failed / 23 skipped**. Opus code review =
**correct + ship-ready, no blocking issues**: verified oracle parity exactly, ran probe tests
for negatives (−1000.01/50-50 conserves), duplicate (source,target) rows, Σpct=120% on $0.01
(no opposite-sign pool), 0% target, source-as-own-target; confirmed SQL injection-safe + org-scoped
+ EOPT-clean. 3 non-blocking NITs (added the source-as-own-target test pre-merge).

**Shipped:** branch fix/c22-pool-allocation-splits-engine (3b138d18) → merged --no-ff to master
**10614134** → pushed origin/master. Deployed capveri-api version
`744cf783-23de-497a-9442-bdaaf8825805` (100%), health `{"status":"healthy",...}`.

unmatched-GL DB-column persistence + suspense-pool routing; pool-mapping >100% write-path

## Cycle 25: getSnapshot Date-decode fix (porsager `select *` contract violation)

**Shipped:** master `bcfcb9eb` (pushed) · capveri-api deploy `cc652c68-b61c-4ad1-8d8e-69d42d6aed32`
(100%, `/health` 200 healthy).

**The bug (REAL, the single shippable finding of the C24/C25 sweeps).**
`getSnapshot` (reconciliation.ts:525) reads with a bare `select *` (no `::text` cast) and
post-processes the row through `normalizeSnapshotJsonFields` (reconciliation.ts:1415). Per
the established CF-postgres-Date-decode footgun (commit a9ebf6d9), porsager/postgres.js
decodes bare `date`/`timestamptz` columns into JS `Date` objects. So at runtime the four
fields `period_start_date`, `period_end_date` (date) and `finalized_at`, `created_at`
(timestamptz) arrive as `Date`, **violating** the `ReconciliationSnapshotRecord` type which
declares them `string` / `string | null`. Two reachable consequences:

1. **Finalize-results email silently never sent.** The finalize handler builds the email URL
   via `reconciliationUrl(...)`, which does `period_start_date.slice(0, 4)`
   (reconciliation-routes.ts:857). `.slice` on a `Date` throws `TypeError`, which the
   handler's `swallow()` discards → the landlord's reconciliation-complete notification is
   silently dropped.
2. **GET snapshot-detail emits the wrong date format.** `c.json(snapshot)`
   (reconciliation-routes.ts:280) would serialize a `Date` as a full ISO timestamp
   (`"2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"`) instead of the contract's `"2026-01-01"`.

**Fix (reconciliation.ts:1415).** Coerce the four fields back to their declared string form
inside `normalizeSnapshotJsonFields` (the single getSnapshot post-processing step), reusing
the existing helpers: `period_start_date`/`period_end_date` → `serializeDateOnly`,
`finalized_at`/`created_at` → `serializeOptionalDateTime`. Both gate on `value instanceof
Date`, so already-string rows pass through untouched (idempotent, safe if a future caller
adds a `::text` cast). `serializeDateOnly`'s `toISOString().slice(0,10)` cannot off-by-one
vs a `::text` cast because postgres.js decodes a bare `date` as **UTC-midnight** `Date` and
`toISOString()` is UTC.

**RED-proven regression** (reconciliation-repository.test.ts:254): feeds `Date` objects
through `getSnapshot` via the fake executor and asserts the returned record fields are the
expected `YYYY-MM-DD` / ISO strings. Proven RED (returned `2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`),
GREEN after fix. Full gate: vitest **1779 passed** / 23 skipped, tsc 0, eslint 0.

**Scope is accurate (not over-claimed).** The other snapshot read paths
(`getSnapshotForErp`/`getSnapshotForPdf` etc. in exports.ts) already `::text`-cast their
date columns and never had the bug; `getSnapshot` was the lone bare-`select *` path
returning a `ReconciliationSnapshotRecord`. Opus code review: clean, no blockers.

**C24/C25 finder triage (no other shippable bugs).** Finder 5 BUG-CF-1 (campaign flip
`succeeded > 0`) = exact oracle parity (reconciliation.py:1217), orphan-remediation gated by
finalized-snapshot existence not campaign status → false positive. Finder 6 RLS "HIGH ×3" =
not exploitable (triple-defended: route gate + partial query scope + DB-enforced RLS;
Worker is RLS-subject). Finder 8 BUG-YOY-1 = Python historical_analysis.py only, Worker
reads stored priority-sorted breakdowns. Finder 9 calculateBillingExposure null-return =
the finalization-email-only EXACT-match surface (commit 41c292de), not the leakage report.

## Cycle 27: Entitlement dollar-gate: tax-protest paywall bypass for expired card-less trials (SHIPPED)

Fresh parallel finder sweep into queue/workflow idempotency, ingestion penny-exactness, and
auth/entitlement dollar gates. Triaged three finders; one shippable real bug surfaced.

**THE BUG (Finder F, CRITICAL, paywall bypass).** `PostgresTaxProtestRepository.hasTaxProtestAccess`
(`cloudflare-backend/src/adapters/db/tax-protest.ts`) gated the premium tax-protest feature
through a file-local `effectiveSubscriptionStatus` that returned `"trialing"` for ANY trialing
row, ignoring `stripe_subscription_id`. So an **expired card-less trial** (`status="trialing"`,
`stripe_subscription_id=null`, `current_period_end` in the past) resolved to `"trialing"` and
**bypassed the paywall** on `POST /api/v1/tax-protest/generate`. The local helper also carried a
**non-canonical `past_due` 7-day grace** that no other premium gate honors.

**RESEARCH / why the fix is toward-correct (not just parity).** No Python oracle exists for this
feature (Worker-only). The canonical entitlement logic lives in TWO mutually-consistent Worker
files: `billing.ts` (`effectiveSubscriptionStatus`/`effectiveSubscriptionStatusAt`, ~1079-1103)
and `exports.ts` (`effectiveSubscriptionStatus`, ~740-758), both applying the **card-less-expired
check**: a trialing row with no stripe sub whose `current_period_end` has passed → `"paused"`
(no access); every other status passes through unchanged; `past_due` gets nothing. The tax-protest
local copy was the lone outlier. Aligning it means a delinquent/expired-trial org gets identical
entitlement treatment across ALL premium features. Grep confirmed zero callers/tests depended on
the dropped past_due grace.

**THE FIX.** Replaced the local helper with a verbatim mirror of the `exports.ts` canonical
(`status !== "trialing" || stripe_subscription_id || !current_period_end` → pass-through; else
`periodEnd < now ? "paused" : status`). Handles `current_period_end: string | Date | null`
(porsager bare-timestamptz Date-decode footgun) with an `instanceof Date` branch + `Number.isNaN`
fallthrough. Added 5 regression tests (expired card-less trial → false; live card-less trial →
true; stripe-backed trial past period → true; past_due → false; active → true). **RED-proven**:
expired-trial + past_due cases returned `true` before the fix.

**Verification.** vitest 116 files / 1784 passed (+5 new), tsc 0, eslint 0. Opus code review:
**SHIP**: confirmed byte-for-byte logic parity with billing.ts + exports.ts across every status,
correct `string|Date|null` + NaN handling, audit_credits fallback stubbed fail-safe (cannot mask a
regression). master `6e725510c`; capveri-api deployed version `80de8a98` at **100%**, `/health`
healthy.

**PARITY-PROTECTION NOTE.** Three premium gates now share ONE card-less-expired semantic
(billing.ts / exports.ts / tax-protest.ts). If this logic ever changes, change all three together;
do NOT reintroduce a per-feature grace window. Entitlement must be uniform across features.

## Cycle 28: Stripe webhook fail-open paywall bypass (incomplete/unknown → "active")

**THE BUG (paywall bypass, reachable in prod).** `mapSubscriptionStatus` in
`cloudflare-backend/src/http/stripe-webhook-routes.ts` (~1304) folded Stripe subscription statuses
into the Postgres `subscription_status` enum `{trialing, active, past_due, canceled, paused}` but its
`default` branch returned `"active"`. Stripe sends `incomplete` (first payment not settled, e.g.
SCA/3DS pending), `incomplete_expired` (first invoice never paid → dead sub), and may add future
statuses; ALL of these fell through to `default → "active"`. Because the entitlement gate grants on
`active|trialing` only, a user whose payment never succeeded was written as `active` and got full
premium access. Single shared call site (`subscriptionSnapshot:1122`) feeds both
`customer.subscription.created` and `.updated`, so a checkout that fails 3DS (Stripe creates the sub
with `status=incomplete` and fires `customer.subscription.created`) is the live trigger.

**RESEARCH: the correct answer (not the oracle).** The DB enum has only 5 values, so the fold MUST
land in that set. Researched each Stripe status: `incomplete` is *recoverable* (Stripe fires
`subscription.updated → active` once payment settles), so it maps to `past_due` (denies access, stays
recoverable through the same call site). Mapping it to `canceled` would wrongly drop a sub about to
succeed. `incomplete_expired` is terminal → `canceled`. Unknown/future status → **fail closed** to
`past_due` (a paywall must never silently grant access; a wrongly-denied paying user surfaces loudly
and recovers when a recognized status arrives). The Python oracle (`backend/`, non-deployed) shares
the identical `default → active` bug, it is itself wrong here, so we did NOT match it
(divergence-toward-correctness).

**THE FIX.** Added `case "incomplete": return "past_due"`, `case "incomplete_expired": return
"canceled"`, and changed `default` from `"active"` to `"past_due"`. All access-granting statuses
(`active`, `trialing`) plus `past_due`/`canceled`/`paused`/`unpaid` are explicitly cased before the
default, so no legitimate-access sub can reach it. Added 3 RED-proven tests (incomplete →
past_due, incomplete_expired → canceled, unknown status → past_due); each printed `Received:
"active"` before the fix.

**Verification.** vitest 116 files / 1787 passed (+3 new), 23 skipped, tsc 0, eslint 0. Opus code
review: **SHIP**: confirmed the entitlement gate is `active|trialing` only (no past_due grace, per
`analysis.ts:54` / `bootstrap.ts:173-174`), single call site, no spurious trial/paused emails
(those branches fire only on the exact `trialing`/`paused` mapped statuses), null status → default →
past_due (fail closed, correct). master `35d96fec9`; capveri-api deployed version `3c2005a5` at
**100%**, `/health` healthy.

**Finder sweep: contradiction resolved + false positives ruled.** The central blocker from this
cycle's parallel finders was a contradiction over porsager NUMERIC decoding. Read the driver config
(`postgres.ts:38-52`): no custom `types` parser, porsager defaults apply → `NUMERIC` (OID 1700)
decodes to a **JS string** (only `date`/`timestamptz` auto-decode to JS Date). Therefore the orphan
finder's findings 1-A/1-B/1-C/2-A/2-E ("un-cast money columns arrive as floats → IEEE-754 drift")
are **FALSE POSITIVES**: un-cast `NUMERIC` arrives as a string and `Money.parse` / `new
Decimal(str)` consume it losslessly. This is why the only prior decode bug (Cycle 25, commit
a9ebf6d9) was about *dates*, not money.

**Deferred to Cycle 29 (task #31):** (F1/F2, CRIT/HIGH) `customer.subscription.updated` and
`invoice.payment_failed` do unconditional `UPDATE` with no event-`created`-timestamp/version guard →
out-of-order Stripe redelivery can permanently revert a recovered `active` back to `past_due`
(needs an event-timestamp column + WHERE guard; oracle shares the gap). (3-E, MED) extraction
`markProcessing` only guards `completed|failed`, so a job stuck in `processing`/`retrying` after a
Worker crash re-processes on queue redelivery → double LLM extraction. (F4, LOW) invoice amounts
stored via `centsToDollars = cents/100` JS float, likely cosmetically safe (`String(n/100)`
round-trips for integer cents) but violates the never-float canon. (F7, LOW) `upsertSubscription`
on-conflict key is `organization_id`, not `stripe_subscription_id`. A 2nd sub silently replaces the
1st. Finder A F3 (duplicate `subscription.deleted` double-fires analytics) is non-financial, not
pursued.

## Cycle 29: Out-of-order Stripe webhook ordering guard (F1/F2, HIGH), SHIPPED

**THE BUG.** Stripe delivers webhook events at-least-once and WITHOUT ordering guarantees. The four
subscription-mutating writes in `cloudflare-backend/src/adapters/db/stripe-webhooks.ts`
(`upsertSubscription`, `updateSubscriptionByStripeId`, `markSubscriptionCanceled`,
`markSubscriptionPastDue`) did an unconditional `UPDATE ... WHERE stripe_subscription_id=$1` with no
event-timestamp high-water mark. A stale/redelivered `customer.subscription.deleted` (->canceled) or
`invoice.payment_failed` (->past_due) arriving AFTER a newer `active` event permanently downgrades a
paying customer (lost revenue); the inverse resurrects a canceled sub (access leak). The Python
oracle (`backend/`, non-deployed) shares the same gap.

**THE FIX (migration-first).** New nullable column `subscriptions.stripe_event_ts timestamptz`
(migration `20260629000000_add_subscription_stripe_event_ts.sql`, metadata-only ADD, no rewrite, no
lock, inherits existing RLS). Threaded the Stripe `event.created` high-water mark (unix seconds)
through `StripeWebhookEvent.created` -> `parseStripeWebhookEvent` -> `dispatchStripeEvent`
(`__event_created` injected on the object) -> `readEventTs` helper -> `subscriptionSnapshot.eventTs`
and the two `mark*` call sites (`handleSubscriptionDeleted`, `handleInvoicePaymentFailed` reads it
from the invoice object). Each mutating write now carries the guard
`and (stripe_event_ts is null or $N::timestamptz is null or $N::timestamptz >= stripe_event_ts)` and
`stripe_event_ts = coalesce($N::timestamptz, stripe_event_ts)`. The upsert guards only its
`on conflict do update` branch (the INSERT path always applies, so created/checkout flows are never
skipped). `coalesce` preserves the watermark when an event carries no timestamp, so a later null
event cannot reopen the stale window.

**WHY THIS CAN NEVER FREEZE A LIVE SUB.** The guard rejects ONLY strictly-older events
(`$N < stripe_event_ts`). Equal timestamps (true redelivery), newer events, and a null on either
side all apply. Verified against LIVE Postgres (`REDACTED_SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF`): predicate probe returned
stale->false(skip), newer->true(apply), equal->true(apply), null->true(fail-open); temp-table replay
confirmed a null event applies the status change while `coalesce` preserves the existing watermark.

**Verification.** tsc 0, eslint 0, vitest 117 files / 1794 passed (+7 new: 5 adapter SQL-guard
tests in `stripe-webhooks-ordering.test.ts` + 2 route wiring tests proving `event.created` reaches
the repo), 23 skipped. Migration applied to live DB + column verified (nullable timestamptz). Opus
code review: **SHIP**: no BLOCKER/HIGH; confirmed guard semantics correct for all four cases, full
coverage (no other `subscriptions.status` write bypasses it; `markCheckoutComplete` writes
`organizations`), eventTs plumbing sound, tests genuine (fail on pre-fix code). One MED (no
DB-backed skip integration test). Covered operationally by the live-Postgres predicate/replay
probe. master `74275663a`; capveri-api deployed version `a7cf8a4f` at **100%**, `/health` healthy.

**Remaining Cycle 29 deferred candidates (LOW, not pursued this cycle):** (F4) invoice amounts via
`centsToDollars = cents/100` JS float, likely cosmetic (integer-cents round-trip) but violates
never-float canon. (F7) `upsertSubscription` on-conflict key is `organization_id` not
`stripe_subscription_id`. A 2nd sub silently replaces the 1st. (3-E) extraction `markProcessing`
re-process: RULED NOT-A-BUG: `markCompleted` CAS `WHERE status in ('processing','retrying')` makes
re-running a `processing` job data-safe (intended crash recovery).

## Cycle 30: Billing money + proration + webhook-concurrency sweep (CLEAN / all findings triaged out)

**Date:** 2026-06-29
**Scope:** Four parallel forensic finders over the highest-risk untouched billing surfaces:
(A) audit-credit / overage billing money; (forensic) invoice/refund/credit money path;
(B) trial-email + webhook-claim idempotency & concurrency races; (C) subscription period /
proration / quantity correctness.

**Outcome: CLEAN.** Every HIGH/BLOCKER from all four finders was adversarially verified against
the real source and resolves to a false positive, unreachable-latent, theoretical, or a
non-money display discrepancy. No fix warranted.

**Verified triage:**
- **B#1/#2 "double trial email + full side-effect replay" (BLOCKER): FALSE POSITIVE.**
  `subscription_email_events` has a unique `(stripe_subscription_id, email_type)` claim row.
  `releaseTrialEmail` (DELETE) only fires in the send-**failure** branch (email not sent), so a
  redelivery re-claims and sends exactly once. When the send **succeeds**,
  `completeTrialEmail` failure throws `PreserveWebhookClaimError`, which the route's outer catch
  (stripe-webhook-routes.ts:142) honors by NOT releasing the webhook claim → no replay. The email
  is sent at most once on every path.
- **B#4 "crm_events duplication" (HIGH): FALSE POSITIVE.** `crm.recordEvent` runs only after a
  successful send, behind the surviving claim row; a redelivery's `claimTrialEmail` returns null
  (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) and short-circuits, so it never re-runs.
- **B#3 `completeTrialEmail` missing `AND status='processing'` guard: defensive-only, unreachable.**
  Runs ≤once per (sub,email_type) successful send given the claim protocol.
- **C#2/#5 `building_count` stale (metadata vs item.quantity) (HIGH): NOT money/entitlement.**
  The charge and overage derive from `unit_count` (`getAnnualTotalCents(tier, unit_count)` +
  `Math.max(unit_count - included_units, 0)` at billing-routes.ts:784/805). `building_count` is a
  descriptive plan-selection/display field, never an entitlement gate (no `properties > building_count`
  comparison exists). Fix direction is ambiguous regardless.
- **A/forensic/C `centsToDollars` float storage: FALSE POSITIVE (3rd confirmation).** Money cols are
  NUMERIC(14,2); porsager returns NUMERIC as string; `/100` is transient JS only and the DB stores
  the exact decimal. No money movement, no penny loss.
- **A#2 `unitPriceCents = floor(amount_total/quantity)`: informational.** Display-only field, never
  re-multiplied to charge; an exact integer cents-per-unit is impossible when total isn't divisible.
- **mapPriceToPlan stub / firstSubscriptionItem `data[0]` / startTrial hardcoded `plan='growth_v2'`:
  latent.** Harmless under the single active plan / single subscription item.
- **C#1 `new Date()` period fallback / `unixSecondsToIso(0)` / `trialChargeDate` anchor fallback:
  theoretical.** Stripe always supplies `current_period_start/end`, `created`, `trial_end` on real
  subscription events; reachable only via malformed/test payloads.
- **REAL-BUT-LOW (documented, not fixed):** `subscription_started` PostHog event can double-fire if a
  side effect AFTER it (e.g. the trial email send) transiently fails and triggers
  `releaseWebhookEvent` (hard DELETE) → Stripe redelivery re-runs `handleSubscriptionCreated` from the
  top. Analytics funnel hygiene only, no money, no user-facing effect. A correct fix (deterministic
  PostHog `$insert_id` dedup, or not releasing the claim after non-idempotent emits) is broader/riskier
  than the LOW severity warrants. Left as a known-LOW.

**Verdict:** The webhook idempotency machinery (per-event claim row + per-email claim row +
`PreserveWebhookClaimError`-after-side-effect) is sound. Billing money path stores exact decimals and
delegates all payment math to Stripe. No code change. master stays at f57ab9443.

## Cycle 31: Cross-tenant RLS isolation + auth/party-guard boundary (CLEAN, both finders)

**Date:** 2026-06-29
**Scope:** Two parallel forensic finders over the multi-tenant security boundary, an area never
swept by prior cycles: (A) cross-tenant data leakage at the query layer (IDOR / missing org filters /
RLS bypass); (B) auth/authorization boundary (tenant→landlord escalation, client-controlled authority,
privilege escalation).

**Outcome: CLEAN both directions.** No exploitable cross-tenant leak, no tenant→landlord escalation,
no privilege escalation, no client-controlled authority. The two finders cross-corroborate: Finder A's
"no leak" rests on route guards being universally present, which Finder B independently confirmed.

**Finder A (data layer): no leak.** Audited ~20 high-risk read/aggregate repos; every org-scoped
query binds `organization_id` directly or filters by a `property_id`/`lease_id`/`snapshot_id` proven
org-bounded earlier in the same request. 3 flagged items chased to ground = false positives
(tax-protest `loadExportContext` leaseId comes from an org-validated snapshot; cross-doc-analysis
guarded by `checkPropertyInOrg`; ingestion `listPropertyPools` is an internal helper behind
`propertyExists`).

**ARCHITECTURAL FINDING (verified by me directly in `adapters/db/postgres.ts`): RLS is INERT for the
Worker's business queries.** Business repos use `createDirectPostgresExecutor(env)` and call
`.query()`/`.transaction()` directly, they never route through `DirectPostgresAdapter.withActorTransaction`,
so they set no `app.*` GUCs and no `request.jwt.claim.sub`. The Hyperdrive/`DATABASE_URL` connection
role bypasses the `auth.uid()`-keyed RLS policies (queries return data with `auth.uid()` unset).
`withActorTransaction` is used only by the demo `ProtectedRecord` repo. **NOT a vulnerability**: it's
the trust model: the Worker path is protected by app-layer `WHERE organization_id` + route guards
(proven clean), and any direct-client/supabase-js path is still protected by the `auth.uid()` RLS
policies (actively maintained per `20240101000035_fix_get_user_org_id_bypass_rls.sql`). Worth a
defense-in-depth hardening RECOMMENDATION (push `organization_id` into leaf queries like pool-config /
cross-doc-analysis / tax-protest that delegate the boundary entirely to the route layer, or make RLS
functional Worker-side), but that is a high-blast-radius refactor, not an autonomous cycle fix, and
fixes no live bug.

**Finder B (auth layer): clean.** Trust root: JWT verified vs remote JWKS, algorithms pinned
ES256/RS256 (blocks alg:none + HS256 confusion), aud+iss enforced in prod. Authority 100% server-derived
in `resolveUserContext` (org/role/party from `users` keyed by verified `sub`; `party==="tenant"` iff
`role==="tenant"`); never from body/header/claim. Party guard default-deny (`DEFAULT_ALLOWED_PARTIES =
["landlord"]`); only 3 route groups opt tenants in (tenant-disputes, tenant-portal, auth-lifecycle), all
session-scoped to tenant-owned rows, no tenant-reachable route mutates landlord recon/billing/settings/
exports/member/extraction data (BLOCKER case absent). Privilege escalation closed: `assignableRoleSchema`
excludes `owner`, `assertManageableMember` throws on owner target, self role-change/remove blocked,
`/team/invitations/accept` requires `actor.userId === body.user_id` + email match + wrong_org guard.
Client-controlled-authority grep clean (only `body.user_id` equality-checked + `body.role` constrained
within admin's own org). 6 unauthenticated routes all have compensating controls (HMAC/Svix/Turnstile+
rate-limit/nonce). All 49 `src/http/` files accounted for.

**Verdict:** Multi-tenant boundary holds in both directions. No fix. master stays at 45c81de76.
Carry-forward RECOMMENDATION (user decision, not autonomous): make Worker-side RLS functional or push
org_id into the route-guard-delegating leaf queries for defense-in-depth.

## Cycle 33: FIX: XLSX billing-import sparse-grid DoS (CWE-400) [master 95e529165]

Realized the Cycle 32 DEFERRED item. `POST /actual-billed/upload` → `parseBillingXlsx`
(billing-parser.ts) read every row across the FULL spanned column width
(`Math.max(actualColumnCount, columnCount)`), so a single far-right cell at column
16384 forced the dense per-row loop to O(rows × 16384). With a genuinely tall sheet
this exhausts the Worker CPU budget on an untrusted upload, the route only caps the
*compressed* file at 25MB (actual-billed-routes.ts:513).

**Research correction to the deferred plan:** the real amplifier dimension is
`actualRowCount` (populated rows = the `eachRow({includeEmpty:false})` iteration count),
NOT the spanned `rowCount` (max index). Confirmed in exceljs/lib/doc/worksheet.js:
`rowCount`=`_lastRowNumber` (cheap for a sparse-tall attacker), while `eachRow` walks the
sparse `_rows` array and SKIPS holes, so a lone cell at row 1,000,000 yields
`actualRowCount===1` and the loop runs once. Bounding `rowCount` would false-reject a
legitimately sparse small file and miss the true cost driver. The opus reviewer independently
verified this against the ExcelJS source and ruled a `rowCount`-based guard WRONG.

**Fix** (billing-parser.ts): before the read loop:
- reject if `worksheet.actualRowCount > MAX_BILLING_ROWS` (100_000) with a clear error;
- clamp `columnCount = Math.min(Math.max(actualColumnCount, columnCount), MAX_BILLING_COLUMNS)` (256).
Worst case is now O(actualRowCount × 256). Real CAM/Yardi/MRI billing files are a handful
of columns and at most a few thousand tenant rows (largest portfolios = low thousands of
leases), so neither limit rejects legitimate input, the parser selects tenant/amount/suite
by header name and those are always leftmost.

**Scoped OUT (platform-bounded LOW, documented in-code):** zip-bomb decompression inside
`workbook.xlsx.load()` runs BEFORE these guards and ExcelJS exposes no streaming/size hook.
Backstopped by the 25MB compressed cap + Cloudflare 128MB isolate memory + per-request CPU
kill → a self-terminating single request, not a durable host-wide DoS. Reviewer concurred LOW.

**CSV path left unchanged (cited clean):** parseCsvRecords is a single O(n) char scan over
text already capped at 25MB; columns emerge from delimiters in the same linear pass, no
sparse-grid multiplier exists.

New `src/test/billing-parser-dos.test.ts` (3 tests): (1) far-right stray cell at col 16384
doesn't corrupt the parse or blow read width (asserts correct 2 rows + $3500 total);
(2) header + 100_001 data rows (100_002 populated > cap) → rejected with "too many rows";
(3) benign 3-column file still parses incl. suite. Initial row-cap test was WRONG (set a
sparse cell at row 100_002 → actualRowCount=2, guard correctly didn't fire), rewrote to
create genuinely-populated rows, which is exactly the dimension the guard bounds.

Gate: tsc 0, eslint 0, full backend suite 1805 passed / 23 skipped / 0 failed. Opus review =
SHIP-WITH-NITS (no blocker; added the one suggested clarifying comment about the pre-load
decompression window before commit). Deploy capveri-api 100% on 579c60ca / api.capveri.com
/health healthy.

## Cycle 36: Mid-period term-version segmentation (Finding 1): scoped, **DECISION-GATED, NOT shipped**

**Verdict: DO NOT autonomously ship. Surface to Angel.** Finding 1 is a real *latent* correctness
gap (zero current production impact, fully reachable in principle), but the fix reshapes the
**universal production billing path's output cardinality**: one `reconciliation_snapshots` row
per lease/period becomes **N rows** (one per term-version segment). The R3 downstream-consumer
audit proves that is **not safe with engine-only changes**: three consumers silently corrupt
under N-rows. This is an outward-facing financial-output change to live customer billing with a
multi-consumer blast radius and no current impact, exactly the class that the non-negotiables
(money correctness) and the confirm-before-hard-to-reverse principle reserve for a human call.

**R3 downstream audit (read-only, agent aba7b69202e2491e8): N-rows-per-lease tolerance:**

SAFE (per-row or correctly-summing): snapshot INSERT (no UNIQUE constraint on
(lease_id, period), plain INSERT…RETURNING, N rows insert fine); snapshot listing (no dedup);
finalizeSnapshot + finalizeBatch (target by snapshot UUID; campaign-flip once per batch);
updateCell (by snapshot id); comparison/variance `loadCorrectByLease` (addToMap SUMS per lease);
variance-pdf `sumRecovery` (per-row reduce); ERP/historical exports (iterate rows); cap-bank
LEDGER `buildCapBankLedger` (receives ALL lease snapshots ordered by period, correct).

SILENTLY-WRONG (must be fixed *with* segmentation, else divergence):
  1. **Cumulative cap-history query**: `loadTenantCapHistories` (reconciliation.ts ~1022-1061):
     `group by lease_id` + `json_agg(... order by period_start_date)` includes EVERY segment, so a
     prior year split into 2 segments injects 2 entries into `priorAmounts` → `yearsSinceBase`
     off-by-N → cumulative cap threshold + bank math wrong, compounding across years. (This is the
     task #39 latent bug, present in BOTH engines today; parity holds ONLY because no prior year
     is segmented yet.) Fix: collapse to one canonical row per (lease, period) before building
     priorAmounts (group by lease_id, period_start, period_end, or pick one term_version per period).
  2. **Denominator-change detector**: `extractDenominatorComponents`
     (denominator-change/service.ts ~293-318): `components.set(leaseId, …)` OVERWRITES, keeping
     only the LAST segment → silent data loss of earlier segments' pro_rata/recovery/excluded_pools;
     callers (`.get(leaseId)`) assume one component per lease. Fix: aggregate segments or key by
     (lease, segment).
  3. **Calculator cap-history map**: calculator.ts ~247-249 (`new Map(... [leaseId, history])`):
     inherits #1's doubled priorAmounts. No code change needed once #1 is fixed.

**Blast radius if approved:** engine (calculator.ts segmentation port + shared proration helper)
+ task #39 cap-history dedup (reconciliation.ts) + denominator-change aggregation
(denominator-change/service.ts), each under the full gate with golden-value tests vs the Python
oracle (`_build_prorated_version_terms` data_fetcher.py:415-466), single-version path kept
byte-identical. No DB UNIQUE constraint blocks N-rows (so no migration is strictly required, but
an index on (lease_id, period_start_date, period_end_date, term_version_id) would back the dedup).

**Status:** Plan agent stopped (executive summary captured; full file-by-file plan deferred,
re-plan on approval to avoid staleness). Tasks #38 (port) + #39 (cap-history) parked
DECISION-GATED pending Angel. Bug-finding loop continues on fresh areas (Cycle 37), this latent
item does not block other coverage.

## Cycle 37: Cap/gross-up/cell-update sweep: 3 HIGH false positives ruled out, 1 LOW shipped (sub-cent input)

**Fresh parallel high-risk hunt over: gross-up reconstruction, multi-year cumulative cap-bank
billing, and the cell-update recompute path. Net ship: one LOW input-validation hardening.
Every HIGH-confidence finder claim was a false positive, all of the same wrong-oracle class.**

### Finder verdicts (all adversarially verified against the LIVE oracle path, not just the named Python fn)

- **Finder A: gross-up base-year asymmetry (claimed HIGH): FALSE POSITIVE.** Premise required a
  `base_year_occupancy` field + active `normalize_base_year` gross-up of the base year. Verified:
  `base_year_occupancy` exists ONLY in `backend/` + docs, never in the production schema/migrations;
  `normalize_base_year` (base_year.py:221) is called ONLY in tests, never in `orchestrator.py`. The
  LEDGER already files this as LOW/unreachable. `base_year_amount` is the as-entered normalized
  base-year stop, not a raw un-grossed expense. No fix.

- **Finder B BUG #1: cumulative cap with missing base "silently returns uncapped vs Python raise"
  (claimed HIGH): FALSE POSITIVE.** Finder compared `calculator.ts:1186-1188` against
  `caps.py:641-642` (`apply_cap` raises ValueError). But the live orchestrator calls
  `tenant_share.calculate_tenant_share`, which at lines 575-597 (FIX FC-7 / bug #17) intercepts the
  "cumulative cap + no historical base" case and downgrades it to `CapType.NONE` (skip cap, return
  uncapped) BEFORE `apply_cap` is ever reached. The `caps.py` raise is unreachable in the live flow.
  Worker's `return amount` is a faithful port, the in-code comment (calculator.ts:1181-1185) already
  documented this. Not a bug.

- **Finder B BUG #2: cumulative cap with missing cap_rate "early-returns uncapped vs Python raise"
  (claimed HIGH): FALSE POSITIVE / unreachable.** A cumulative cap with null `cap_rate` is rejected
  at BOTH HTTP ingestion schemas: `core-data-routes.ts:207` and `recovery-profile-schema.ts:68-71`
  ("cap_rate is required when cap_type is not none"). The `!terms.capRate` guard at
  `calculator.ts:1168` is correct defense-in-depth for a state the validated API cannot produce.
  Not a bug.

- **Finder C #1 (before_cap doesn't cascade) & #2 (override locks recalc): NOT BUGS (by design).**
  The cell grid is a manual-override surface; only `total_recovery = tenant_share_after_cap +
  admin_fee` is auto-maintained (and only when no manual `total_recovery` override exists). #2 is
  explicitly test-pinned as intentional ("preserves an explicit total recovery override"). Verified
  in `reconciliation.ts` `calculateDependentTotalRecovery` (1156-1190).

### Shipped (Finder C #3: LOW, input-validation hardening)

`cellUpdateSchema` (reconciliation-routes.ts:107-125) accepted any decimal precision
(`/^\d+(\.\d+)?$/`). The seven editable columns are all `NUMERIC(14,2)`, so Postgres silently
rounded sub-cent input (e.g. "100.125" → "100.13"); the stored/echoed value then mismatched what the
client submitted, and the rejection message ("Cell value must be non-negative") was inaccurate for a
too-many-decimals case. **Fix:** tighten to `/^\d+(\.\d{1,2})?$/` + accurate message ("…non-negative
number with at most 2 decimal places") + regression test asserting 422 on "100.125". Billing identity
was already penny-exact (PG round-half-away and JS HALF_UP agree for positives), so the only impact
closed is the transient API-echo round-trip mismatch and the misleading error. Gate: tsc 0, eslint 0,
vitest reconciliation-routes 21/21. Review (agent a5b89687) CLEAN. Direct-to-master.

**Durable lesson (reinforced):** when a finder claims "Worker returns X but Python raises", the
named Python fn (`caps.py`) is rarely the live oracle. Trace the ACTUAL orchestrator entry
(`tenant_share.calculate_tenant_share`), it routinely intercepts/downgrades degenerate inputs
(missing base, missing rate, year-1) BEFORE the low-level fn that raises. A `return amount` in the
Worker that mirrors a `CapType.NONE` downgrade is parity, not a bug. 3-of-3 HIGH claims this cycle
died on this exact check.

**Status:** Tasks #38/#39 remain DECISION-GATED (Cycle 36 segmentation, awaiting Angel). Bug-finding
loop continues on fresh areas.

## Cycle 38: Over/under-billing diff, pool-allocation-at-scale, dispute/credit money: NO new ship (1 DECISION-GATED, 2 clean)

**3 parallel finders; net ship = 0. One finalization-email inconsistency surfaced as DECISION-GATED
(deliberate, test-pinned behavior whose correctness depends on product-workflow intent), two clean.**

### Finder A: actual-billed vs computed exposure diff: claimed CRITICAL, ruled DECISION-GATED (deliberate design)

Finder claimed `loadBillingExposureDataset` (actual-billed.ts:372-427) is a port error: it joins
`reconciliation_snapshots` and `actual_billed_amounts` on **exact** period (`period_start_date = $3
and period_end_date = $4`) while the sibling leakage feature `loadLeakageDataset` (actual-billed.ts:270-340)
uses **overlap** (`period_start_date <= $4 and period_end_date >= $3`). Since `actual_billed_amounts`
periods are user-supplied and independent (actual-billed-routes.ts:36-37/75-79, validated only start<end),
exact-match silently drops actuals whose period doesn't equal the reconciliation period (e.g. monthly
invoices vs an annual reconciliation): `calculateBillingExposure` (billing-exposure.ts) returns `null`
when `billedRows` is empty, so the finalization email omits/understates exposure.

**Why NOT a bug to autonomously fix:** the exact-match is **explicitly, intentionally test-pinned**:
`actual-billed-routes.test.ts:1133` is titled *"loads exposure comparison data using exact finalized and
billed periods"* and asserts the queries DO use `= $3/$4` and explicitly do NOT contain `<=`/`>=`
(lines 1168-1174). This is a deliberate 1:1 period-paired comparison for the finalization email, distinct
by design from the leakage report's arbitrary-window overlap. Whether exact-pairing is financially correct
depends on the intended actual-billed upload workflow (totals keyed to the reconciliation period =>
exact-match right, overlap would over-sum sub-period rows; vs monthly-invoice cadence => exact-match drops
them). That is a product/domain decision, not a code-provable one. **Real surfaceable observation:** the
finalization email (exact) can disagree with the leakage page (overlap) for the same property+period, a
user-visible inconsistency. **Impact is confined to the finalization notification email's exposure summary;
tenant billing math is untouched (MED at most).** Outward-facing + ambiguous + test-pinned => surface to
Angel, do NOT autonomously flip the pinned contract. Parked as task #42.

### Finder B: pool-allocation largest-remainder at scale: CLEAN (Worker already MORE correct than oracle)

Only divergence found is the Python oracle being LESS correct: `pool_allocation.py` `_largest_remainder`
sorts by a Decimal fractional remainder, which on mathematically-equal fractions can compare unequal at
high dp => unstable tie-break order. The Worker (calculator.ts:790-831) uses an INTEGER remainder
(`numerator % totalWeight`) => stable, index-tie-broken, sum-to-total exact. Both sum to total, no tenant
overbilling, per-pool detail can differ by 1 cent. Per the research mandate (divergence-toward-correctness)
the Worker is correct; "fixing" it to match Python would make it worse. **No Worker change.**

### Finder C: tenant-dispute / credit / refund / adjustment money: CLEAN

Disputes are workflow/communication records only, `disputes`/`dispute_comments`/`dispute_attachments`
have NO amount/credit/debit/settlement/adjustment columns; dispute resolution triggers no snapshot
recompute or balance change. No money path exists to carry a sign error, double-application, or drift.
RLS/party-guard sound (tenant routes scope by tenant_user_id AND organization_id; admin routes require
landlord party + requireAdmin + requireFullAccess). No fix.

**Status:** Cycle 38 net ship = 0. Task #42 (finalization-email exact-vs-overlap exposure) parked
DECISION-GATED pending Angel (alongside #38/#39). Loop continues on fresh areas. **DURABLE LESSON
(reinforced, now 5x): a HIGH "port error" claim must be checked against the TARGET function's own tests.
An intentionally-titled pinning test ("…using exact … periods" + explicit `not.toContain('<=')`) means the
behavior is a design decision, not a port bug. Also: when two sibling functions answer different questions
(finalization 1:1 period pairing vs leakage arbitrary-window overlap), divergent SQL is expected, not a bug.**

`reconciliation_snapshots` has NO unique constraint on (lease_id, period_start_date, period_end_date),

re-run-over-already-finalized case.

REDACTED_SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF): 44 snapshots / 5 finalized / 39 draft, **ZERO duplicate (lease, period) rows for either
status**. The race has NEVER fired. The proper fix is a DB unique constraint, which (a) is a high-blast schema

## Cycle 40: Money arithmetic / billing-entitlement / date-period pivot: 1 MED billing fix SHIPPED, engine-adjacent surfaces clean

**Pivoted off the now-well-covered reconciliation engine (two prior near-zero cycles) to thinner surfaces.
3 parallel finders. Net: 1 real MED idempotency bug fixed + shipped to prod; 2 finders clean.**

### Finder A: money.ts low-level arithmetic: CLEAN

Read money.ts in full, constructed extreme-magnitude / rounding-boundary / negative / parse scenarios, and
HONESTLY withdrew every candidate finding. Confirmed correct: Money/Rate are bigint internally so the 2^53
precision class does NOT apply to any stored value or to add/subtract/multiplyRate/Rate.multiply intermediates
(bigint products are exact at any magnitude); roundDivide correctly implements round-half-away-from-zero, which
matches Python Decimal.quantize(ROUND_HALF_UP) on BOTH signs (-2.5 to -3, +2.5 to +3), the calc oracle's
intended mode (pinned reconciliation-repository.test.ts:561); single-guard-digit parse rounding (3rd digit for
Money cents, 9th for Rate) is mathematically sufficient for HALF_UP; negatives in min/max/gt/gte/subtract operate
on signed bigint correctly; no abs() drops a sign in a result path; toString collapses -0n to "0.00". Strongest
non-breaking scenario: Money.parse("92233720368547758.07").multiplyRate(Rate.parse("0.33333333")), exact bigint,
where a number-based impl would lose precision above 2^53. Lone caveat (MED to LOW, NOT shipped): the parse regex
/^-?\d+(\.\d+)?$/ THROWS on scientific-notation strings (String(n) for |n|>=1e21), a latent crash only if a caller
ever passes a raw large/small JS number instead of a decimal DB string, none do today.

### Finder B: billing/entitlement/Stripe money: 1 MED SHIPPED + LOW/CLEAN

**SHIPPED (master 8dd045721, pushed; capveri-api 100% b970b54f, /health healthy).** POST
/billing/save-offer/:attemptId/accept (billing-routes.ts:569-621) fetched the attempt by id+org only
(getSaveOfferAttempt has no offer_accepted-is-null filter) and NEVER checked attempt.offer_accepted, then
unconditionally called stripeApplySubscriptionCoupon (POSTs coupon onto the live subscription) +
markSaveOfferAccepted (unconditional UPDATE). So re-POSTing accept re-applied the retention coupon every call; for
a once-duration "20% off one invoice" coupon that re-grants the discount on the next invoice each billing period,
a repeatable, owner-gated revenue leak. Verified vs source: migration 20260224000002 has offer_accepted BOOLEAN
(nullable); no existing test pinned re-accept as allowed (the "rejects unavailable…" test only covers
missing-attempt 404 + non-discount-offer 400). Fix: reject with 409 save_offer_already_accepted when
attempt.offer_accepted === true, BEFORE any Stripe mutation; + regression test asserting the subscription is not
touched on a replayed accept. Gate tsc/eslint 0, vitest 84/84. Other findings: LOW (hasFullAccess ignores credits
when a non-credit_pack sub row exists, fails CLOSED, UX-only) and LOW (invoice status writes lack the event-ts
high-water guard that subscription writes have, but entitlement keys off subscription status, so cosmetic).
Verified CLEAN with strongest non-breaking scenarios: webhook idempotency (claimWebhookEvent
on-conflict-do-nothing + insertAuditCredits on-conflict(session_id), replay can't double-grant); out-of-order
subscription status (all 4 writers carry stripe_event_ts >= high-water guard); money-back guarantee double-refund
(idempotency key + conditional where money_back_claimed_at is null returning id); entitlement fail-CLOSED;
tier-band math contiguous/non-overlapping; usage counting (no decrement path by design = nothing to off-by-one).

No CRITICAL/HIGH Worker-introduced date bug. Hot paths correctly UTC-anchored + ::text-cast. Verified CORRECT:
proration/occupancy day-count (inclusiveDayCount uses Date.parse(day+T00:00:00Z) both ends + round +1;

diffs (both operands Date.UTC midnight -> exact 86.4M multiples); GL CSV date parsing (UTC round-trip rejects

lookup (meta.storagePath / detail.storageKey / payload.r2Key), never an attacker-supplied key. Scenario tested:
org-B user GETs /disputes/<orgA-disputeId>/attachments/<orgA-attachmentId> -> org-scoped WHERE returns no row ->
404 before any R2 fetch; substituting an attachment id is futile because the storage key is read from the row, not
the URL. Upload validation: content-length pre-check + post-read per-file size guard on EVERY upload route (Cycle 33's
XLSX-DoS fix has propagated uniformly: documents 50MB / disputes 10MB / screenshots 5MB / ingestion 51MB); PDF
magic-byte check; filenames through sanitizeFilename + keys through assertObjectKey (reject ../, null bytes, leading/
trailing slash). Signed URLs: 3 HMAC surfaces all bind (key/documentId, org_id, expires), timing-safe compare, <=1h
TTL, GET-only, org re-checked at DB; feedback/screenshot-file additionally forces key to start with feedback/{org_id}/.
Object keys embed crypto.randomUUID() + org/property namespacing (no collision). Extends Cycle 31/33; no re-land.

### Finder A: billing/subscription lifecycle state machine: 1 HIGH SHIPPED + 1 HIGH surfaced + 1 LOW

**SHIPPED (master f8d15bd8c, pushed; capveri-api 100% 8f75495b, /health healthy).** POST /billing/checkout
(billing-routes.ts:1085-1203) only guarded the `paused`-local-row case. An org already holding a LIVE Stripe
subscription (active/trialing/past_due with stripe_subscription_id) passed straight through. Stripe Checkout in
subscription mode ALWAYS creates a SECOND subscription; on completion `upsertSubscription`'s
`on conflict (organization_id) do update` (stripe-webhooks.ts:104) overwrites the row's stripe_subscription_id with
the NEW sub, orphaning the OLD one, which keeps billing the customer with NO in-app way to cancel it (cancel/resume
read the row's now-overwritten id). Verified vs source: the /billing/checkout/success handler (1205-1231) does NOT
cancel the prior sub (only echoes ids); there is no "has ever subscribed" ledger (has_ever_purchased = credit-packs
only); `resolveTrialDays` (2062) returns full TRIAL_DAYS=30 for an active stripe-backed row, so re-checkout ALSO
re-grants a fresh 30-day trial. = silent double-billing, owner-gated, repeatable. Plan changes are already disabled
(upgrade/downgrade return 400 plan_change_disabled) so the product stance is "changes go through the Stripe billing
portal, not re-checkout": the fix is consistent with that. Fix: reject with 409 `already_subscribed` when
`checkoutState.stripe_subscription_id && status !== "canceled"`, BEFORE any Stripe mutation. `canceled` rows and
null-sub local trials still pass (resubscribe / trial->paid conversion preserved). + 2 regression tests (reject
active re-checkout asserting fetchMock NOT called; allow canceled re-checkout asserting 200 + fetch called). Gate
tsc/eslint 0, vitest 86/86.

**SURFACED: HIGH (NOT shipped, policy-gated → task):** canceled org can re-arm an UNLIMITED fresh 30-day local
trial via POST /billing/trial/start. startTrial (billing.ts:203-291) only blocks `paused`; a `canceled` row passes
the shouldUpsertLocalTrial gate (existingStatus !== "active" && !(trialing && stripe_sub)) → upserts a fresh
trialing row, current_period_end = now+30d → hasFullAccess returns true → 30 days free premium, no card, repeatable
every time the org reaches canceled. Real revenue-leak risk BUT the fix is a PRODUCT-POLICY decision (one-trial-per-org
forever vs. intentional winback re-trial) and requires a has_ever_trialed ledger we don't have. Not autonomously
shippable. Surfaced to Angel.

**LOW (NOT shipped):** getFreeAuditStatus (billing.ts:293-324) treats a past_due (lapsed) payer like a brand-new
free user (can_run_reconciliation = !startedFreeAudit), but the hard money gate requireFullAccess/hasFullAccess
stays CLOSED for past_due, so it's a gate-disagreement / UX inconsistency, not a paid-feature leak.

**Structural negatives (ruled out whole categories honestly):** subscriptions.organization_id is UNIQUE + every
writer uses on conflict (organization_id) → "duplicate rows / which row does hasFullAccess pick" is structurally
impossible (always exactly one row). Proration/plan-change money does not exist as code (upgrade/downgrade hard-return
400). mapSubscriptionStatus fails closed (incomplete/unknown -> past_due). Out-of-order webhook high-water guard
(C29) intact. cancel-at-period-end keeps access until subscription.deleted (correct). Strongest non-breaking
sequences all held.
