## Cycle 44: Recon snapshot write atomicity + CRM/lead idempotency + credit-grant webhook reordering: 1 atomicity fix SHIPPED, rest decision-gated / false-positive

**3 parallel finders. Net: 1 real fail-closed atomicity fix shipped (no happy-path change) + 4 decision-gated surfaces + 1 adversarially-disproven false positive. Finder deflection cascade fought off via SendMessage "STOP delegating, output findings directly".**

### Finder A: recon snapshot write atomicity: REAL, SHIPPED (master 4e9d3cc90; capveri-api 100% ace06b5c, /health healthy)

The queue runner (`workflows/reconciliation.ts run()`) persisted a finished calculation as THREE separate non-transactional statements: deleteDraftSnapshots (force_recalculate) → insertCalculationSnapshots (a per-snapshot `for` loop of bare INSERTs) → completeCalculationJob. Verified at source: `adapters/db/reconciliation.ts` insertCalculationSnapshots (was 372-425) is a bare loop, completeCalculationJob (was 427-447) a separate query, NO transaction anywhere; contrast finalizeBatch which correctly wraps in `executor.transaction()` + `FOR UPDATE`. **Real outcome:** a failure midway through the insert loop (conn drop / one row throws) commits an INCOMPLETE subset of `draft` snapshots while the catch marks the job `failed`. Those orphaned partial rows are (a) viewable in listSnapshots as if a real reconciliation, (b) individually finalizable via finalizeSnapshot (billing tenants off an incomplete reconciliation), and (c) block a non-force retry via the draft-exists guard. **Fix** = new `ReconciliationRepository.persistCalculationResults` wrapping delete+insert+complete in one `executor.transaction()`, reusing the existing SQL via 3 module-level executor-param helpers (deleteDraftSnapshotRows / insertCalculationSnapshotRows / completeCalculationJobRow) mirroring the finalizeBatch free-function style. Compute runs BEFORE the tx opens (short tx); the draft delete moved inside the tx is safe because loadCalculationDataset never reads current-period drafts (cap histories come from prior-year FINALIZED snapshots). All-or-nothing now: full set lands + job completes, or nothing persists + job fails with no orphans. No happy-path behavior change. The finalized-period guard stays a pre-tx read, its TOCTOU is the separately-tracked #44 (duplicate-finalized-snapshot race, needs a schema change). Gate: tsc 0, eslint 0, vitest 39/39 (+2 new: single-atomic-call assertion on happy path; force_recalculate deletes within the atomic call). Updated 3 full-mock impls + the interface.

### Finder B: CRM/lead-capture/marketing pipeline idempotency: 1 MED + 3 LOW, all decision-gated/by-design

- **Finding 1 (MED) → task #53 (decision-gated, migration-first).** content_leads dedup is a non-atomic check-then-insert (hasRecentLead SELECT exists → bare insert, NO on-conflict, no unique constraint). Two same-tick POSTs (same email+asset_slug) → 2 lead rows + 2 download emails + 2 PostHog events (sequencer enroll keys on the per-row leadId so it does NOT collapse). Fix = partial unique index + `on conflict do nothing returning id` mapped to the existing 429. Gated: uniqueness window is a policy choice; live outward-facing funnel; CREATE UNIQUE INDEX fails if prod dups already exist (must inspect+dedupe first).
- **Finding 2 (LOW/MED) decision-gated.** Public lead routes have no IP/global rate limit; only per-email throttle (trivially bypassed via plus/dot email variants) → self-spam Resend cost-abuse + CRM/analytics inflation. Mechanism exists (DurableObjectContactRateLimiter, already used by contact route), wiring an IP-keyed `lead:${ip}` check is low-blast but the limit value is policy. (DoS-class; lifted above pure-LOW only because it corrupts lead/analytics data.)
- **Finding 3 (LOW) schema-gated.** /auth/welcome welcome-email send + signup_completed crm_event are not idempotent (nurture events + sequencer enroll ARE). Double POST → 2 welcome emails. Needs a "welcome already sent" marker column (claim row), small schema add, self-only harm.
- **Finding 4 (LOW, by-design CLEAN).** crm_events ledger has no dedup key (immutable event log, intentional). Dedup must live at the action layer (Findings 1/3), not the ledger.
- **CLEAN verified:** cross-tenant/RLS scoping on crm_contacts/crm_events/content_leads/email_suppressions (app-owned global tables, deny-all authenticated policies, service_role-only, coalesce upsert avoids wrong-org overwrite); HTML/email injection (every user value through escapeHtml/escapeAttr incl. firstName via paragraph() default-escape); CSV/formula injection (no lead CSV export); PII-to-analytics (cleanAnalyticsProperties strips email/name/phone; SHA-256 lead distinct_id); Turnstile + honeypot fail-closed on all routes.

### Finder C: credit-grant webhook reordering: BUG A FALSE POSITIVE (adversarially disproven), BUG B = #52, BUG C LOW

- **BUG A (claimed HIGH): FALSE POSITIVE, proven.** Sub-agent claimed all ~14 entitlement gates check `credits_purchased > 0` instead of `credits_remaining > 0` → "drained pack still grants access" money leak. Adversarial verification per research mandate: grepped the entire Worker for any `UPDATE ... credits_used` / `credit_consumption_log` writer. NONE exists. insertAuditCredits hardcodes `credits_used` to 0 (stripe-webhooks.ts:316 `values ($1,$2,0,...)`). Therefore `credits_remaining ≡ credits_purchased` for every row, always; the two checks are mathematically identical and the "drain" scenario cannot occur. The credit pack is a one-time license (has_ever_purchased), NOT a metered balance. Changing the gate would be a cargo-cult no-op. NOT shipped. (Matches top-level Finder C's "no spend path" conclusion; the sub-agent's framing was wrong.)
- **BUG B = re-discovery of #52** (credit-pack refund/chargeback does not claw back paid access), decision-gated, already tracked.
- **BUG C (LOW observability)**: handleCheckoutSessionCompleted discards insertAuditCredits' "inserted"|"duplicate" return; could log a duplicate-grant line. Not worth an autonomous ship.
- **CLEAN:** replay double-grant blocked by dual idempotency (event-id claim `on conflict do nothing` + session-id UNIQUE `on conflict do nothing`); single writer to audit_credits; integer cents; DB CHECK + GENERATED column.

**Status:** Cycle 44 shipped 1 fail-closed atomicity fix (the only unambiguous, no-normal-behavior-change defect). DURABLE LESSONS: (a) a multi-write persistence path with no `executor.transaction()` wrapper is a partial-write hazard, grep workflow/queue runners for sequential repository mutation calls that aren't wrapped; the fix mirrors the finalizeBatch free-function-takes-executor pattern, compute-before-tx to keep the tx short. (b) An entitlement gate "money leak" that hinges on a balance being DRAINED is a false positive unless a spend path actually writes the consumption column, verify the writer exists (grep `UPDATE ... <used_col>`) before touching ~N gates; `credits_remaining` generated-column ≡ `credits_purchased` when nothing ever increments used. (c) Lead/CRM dedup correctness lives at the ACTION layer (atomic insert/claim), never the append-only event ledger; check-then-insert without a DB unique constraint is a TOCTOU under concurrent same-tick POSTs.

### Finder A: non-transactional multi-write hazard sweep (generalizing Cycle 44): 1 REAL, SHIPPED (master a943e2738; capveri-api 100% 84e7861b, /health healthy)

`PostgresOnboardingRepository.upgradeUser` (adapters/db/onboarding.ts:73-94) issued TWO sequential, un-wrapped writes: `update users set email` then `update organizations set name`. A failure after the email update committed left a half-applied upgrade (real email but org still named "Anonymous Org"), an asymmetric state only a later retry could heal. Verified at source: no `.transaction(` enclosing the pair, while `initUser` directly above (L18-71) correctly wraps its insert/insert/delete race-recovery flow in `executor.transaction()`. **Fix** = wrap both updates in one `executor.transaction()`, returning state from inside (mirrors initUser). No happy-path behavior change. Gate: tsc 0, eslint 0, onboard-routes.test 8/8 (route test mocks the repository interface, not the executor, so unaffected). Severity MED→ realistically LOW (recoverable, self-only, non-financial, non-cross-tenant) but a zero-risk pattern-aligned fix worth taking.

Finder A's 2nd candidate: `/leads/unsubscribe` (leads-routes.ts:459-466): suppressEmail (idempotent upsert) then markContentLeadsUnsubscribed, ruled **benign, NOT shipped**. The authoritative email gate (email_suppressions) commits FIRST, so a partial failure leaves the user correctly suppressed (won't receive mail = the user's intent); only a secondary reporting marker (content_leads.unsubscribed_at) lags, and a retry heals it. Current ordering is already fail-safe. Verified 13 other multi-write paths CLEAN (all correctly wrapped): persistCalculationResults, finalizeBatch, finalizeSnapshot, updateCell, createLeaseTermVersion, deleteLeaseTermVersion, applyTemplate, copyPools, createDocument, deleteDocument, queueExtraction, approveExtraction, rejectExtraction, markCompleted, markExtractionEnqueueFailed, initUser.

Finder B read full statements, not grep fragments. Ruling holds. No fix.

Exhaustive (61 tool-uses) review of money.ts (Money bigint-cents scale 100, Rate scale 1e8, both ROUND_HALF_UP), calculator.ts (sumMoney integer add; gross-up factor quantized 4dp HALF_UP; MIN_SAFE_OCCUPANCY 0.0001 guard; pro-rata [0,1] validation + zero-sqft guard; chained multiplyRate each rounds to cents; largestRemainder L790-831 conserves to exact total via leftover=total-Σfloors), cumulative-cap.ts (Decimal precision 28, single quantize/year, negative+>100% rate rejection), updateCell recompute (Decimal.plus + toFixed(2,HALF_UP)), comparison/model.ts variance (Decimal .plus/.minus, toFixed only on aggregate), analysis/service.ts (HALF_EVEN intentional for read-only reporting). DURABLE LESSONS: (a) the Cycle-44 non-transactional-multi-write pattern recurs, grep every repository method + route handler for 2+ sequential `executor.query` mutations with no enclosing `.transaction(`; the fix is always "wrap mirroring the sibling that already does it." (b) NOT every un-wrapped multi-write is a real defect, when the writes target different concerns and the FIRST-committed write is the authoritative/fail-safe control (e.g. email suppression before a secondary reporting marker), the partial state is benign and retry-healing; rank by "what bad state results if write #1 commits and #2 fails," not by the mere absence of a transaction. (c) When auditing org-scoping, array-joined SQL means a bare `where id = $1` grep line is NOT proof of missing scope, read the full joined statement; the `and organization_id = $N` is usually the next array element.

NOT auto-shipped: the fix direction is tenant-facing (Option A single-finalize flips campaign → enables INCOMPLETE reconciliations to be sent to tenants; Option B/C completeness-gated flip = only sendable when all property-year snapshots finalized). - **Finding 6 (HIGH claim) → FALSE POSITIVE, adversarially disproven.** Claimed invoice.paid does not reset past_due→active, so a recovered payer stays locked out. (b) "torn read" claims die to two facts: finalize/lifecycle UPDATEs that touch only status/audit columns (never money, money is insert-once) AND MVCC single-statement consistency; verify the UPDATE column set before entertaining a torn-money read. (c) invoice.* events own invoice state, subscription.* events own subscription/entitlement state, a webhook handler that keeps them separate is correct, not buggy; recovery from past_due flows through subscription.updated (Stripe emits it on every status change) + the stripe_event_ts high-water guard, not through invoice.paid. (d) bare-INSERT observability tables (audit_pipeline_events, crm_events) with NO downstream SELECT are benign under queue/HTTP retry, rank by consumer harm, not by the mere absence of ON CONFLICT.

It NEVER touches `calculation_trace`/`trace_checksum`/`engine_version`. Finalize (finalizeSnapshotById:1373) mutates ONLY status/finalized_at/finalized_by, never money OR trace. **Reachable consumer impact:** property PDF (property-pdf.ts, route `GET …/export/pdf`, getSnapshotForPdf is `rs.status='finalized'`-gated) renders BOTH the Expense Summary table from the overridden money COLUMNS (lines 118-140: tenant_share_after_cap L137, admin_fee L139) + the bold Total from overridden total_recovery (L216) (internally consistent) AND a "Calculation Summary" that lists the ENGINE's original `calculation_trace` step output_values (L245-260, stale after any override), with `manual_overrides` disclosed NOWHERE in any export (grep-confirmed absent from exports.ts/erp-formatters/property-pdf). So a tenant PDF can show a step-by-step engine derivation that does not reconcile to the (correct, overridden) billed total, with the manual adjustment invisible. **NOT auto-shipped:** the billed total is CORRECT (override is the intended correction) so this is NOT a fail-closed money fix; the fix is an outward-facing tenant-PDF disclosure/presentation choice with multiple valid options (A: append a "Manual Adjustments" block sourced from manual_overrides; B: annotate the Calculation Summary as engine-reference-only when manual_overrides non-empty; C: re-derive trace = REJECTED, destroys immutable engine evidence; D: accept by-design). Recommended A or B. Decision-gated per the outward-facing/product-intent principle.

So the "stale checksum" half of the claim harms no consumer, the audit chain is intentionally LAYERED (immutable engine trace+checksum as engine evidence + separate manual_overrides as the override record). ## Cycle 48: Cap-bank multi-year billing + GL/rent-roll re-import idempotency + GL numeric fidelity: 1 fail-closed ship (GL amount::text), 2 decision-gated re-upload dups, 1 needs-research cap divergence, rest false-positive/by-design

### SHIPPED: GL `amount::text` cast at 3 lone-outlier reads (master c5184e4c6; capveri-api 100% 6d03deeb, /health healthy)

Both Finder A (Finding 7, HIGH) and Finder B (Finding 1, CRITICAL) **independently converged** on the same site: `gl_entries.amount` is read WITHOUT a `::text` cast at three places: `loadCalculationGlEntries` (reconciliation.ts:898, feeds the CORE reconciliation engine) and the two cross-doc GL aggregations (cross-doc-analysis.ts:444 & 713, feed `new PyDecimal(...)` pool totals). Every OTHER GL-amount read in the codebase casts it: analysis.ts:172, capex.ts:87 & 248, sb1103.ts:475, tax-protest.ts:297 (5 siblings). The reconciliation query at :898 even `::text`-casts its OWN date columns (with an explanatory porsager-decode comment) but forgot `amount`. Downstream consumers (`Money.parse` / `PyDecimal`, both typed `amount: string` with a `?? "0"` string fallback) already assume a precise decimal string.

**Honest severity = LOW/defensive, NOT the claimed CRITICAL.** porsager returns NUMERIC without a built-in JS parser, so realistic CAM money (2dp, well under 2^53 cents) round-trips fine even uncast; precision only bites at absurd magnitudes (>~$90T single GL line). But the fix is an **unambiguous fail-closed pattern-align**: it guarantees the string the consumers already assume, aligns the 3 outliers with 5 siblings + the query's own date casts, can only improve correctness, zero behavior change for realistic values. Gate: tsc 0, eslint 0, cross-doc-analysis-repository + reconciliation-financial-correctness tests 17/17. Shipped.

### Finder B: extraction verify-before-commit + import idempotency: 1 ship (above), 2 FALSE POSITIVE parser findings, 2 decision-gated re-upload dups

- **Finding 3 (HIGH claim: billing-parser parseMoney lacks Unicode-minus U+2212) → FALSE POSITIVE.** & **Finding 6 (MED claim: parseMoney drops "(500.00) CR") → FALSE POSITIVE.** Adversarially disproven by reading the FULL parse path: `parseBillingRecords` (billing-parser.ts:223-229) **rejects zero/negative amounts BY DESIGN** (`if (amount.lte(0)) skip "zero or negative"`). Every format these findings cite (U+2212 "−500", "500 CR", trailing-minus "500-", "(x) CR") represents a NEGATIVE amount → dropped either way; mirroring the GL parser's sign handling would only change the warning string ("not a number" → "zero or negative"), never any billed total or valid-row count. The GL `cleanCurrency` (ingestion/csv-parser.ts:438) accepts signed reversals because GL entries CAN be credits/reductions; the actual-billed importer's contract is POSITIVE billed amounts only. **Different contracts → matching the sibling is NOT correct here.** (The only positive-value gap is £/€/¥ symbols or space thousands-separators, which `cleanCurrency` strips but `parseMoney` doesn't, unrealistic for a US-only Yardi/MRI/USD product; not shipped.) The `amount.lte(0)` positive-only design is itself a pre-existing product choice (should net-credit billed rows be importable?), noted, not a new task (not finder-flagged, established intent).
- **Finding 4 (HIGH: actual-billed re-upload no dedup) → REAL, DECISION-GATED, task #60.** `/actual-billed/upload` → createUploadRows (actual-billed.ts:88) inserts each row with a fresh UUID, no delete-before-insert / file_hash / on-conflict. Re-upload doubles the billed total in over/under-billing comparison. A `deleteBilledAmounts` method exists (:147) but the upload route never calls it. Fix is product/UX-dependent (replace vs file_hash-migration-dedup vs reject vs append+warn; must preserve manual match edits from PUT /actual-billed/matches). Same class as #44/#53.
- **Finding 5 (HIGH: rent-roll re-upload dup property) → REAL, DECISION-GATED, task #61.** rent-roll persists via insertReturning (rent-roll.ts:200), bare INSERT, no on-conflict/match-existing. Re-upload creates a duplicate property+units. Fix is product/UX-dependent (match-and-replace vs version vs reject; no natural dedup key today → schema-touching).
- Verify-before-commit canon re-confirmed HOLDS (consistent with Cycles 42/47).

### Finder A: cap-bank multi-year carryforward billing vs oracle: 1 needs-research divergence (#62), rest by-design/LOW

- **Finding 4 (UNCERTAIN: cap history base_year filter divergence) → NEEDS-RESEARCH, task #62.** Worker's loadTenantCapHistories (reconciliation.ts ~1013) builds priorAmounts from ALL finalized snapshots before the current period (no base_year filter); the Python oracle's data_fetcher (data_fetcher.py:158-169) filters to `period_year >= base_year`. If a cumulative/compounding cap lease has a set base_year with earlier finalized snapshots, the two engines build different cap banks. UNCERTAIN which side is financially correct (oracle may over-filter, or Worker may wrongly include pre-base-year history). Needs CAM research + product intent before changing either side, do NOT assume oracle-parity is correct (research mandate). Related to #38/#39.
- **Finding 2 (MED: 50-yr compounding cap plateau) → BY-DESIGN, no ship.** `Math.min(yearsSinceBase, MAX_YEARS=50)` in cumulative-cap.ts:143 is a faithful port of the oracle's FIX FC-2 overflow guard (caps.py:440-444, same value). Both plateau identically → no divergence; only a >50-year-lease theoretical concern, matches oracle. Not a Worker defect.
- **Finding 3/5 (LOW: Money.parse accepts >2dp) → LOW/defensive, no ship.** money.ts regex `/^-?\d+(\.\d+)?$/` permits >2dp and silently rounds. In practice every Money value comes from a `::text`-cast NUMERIC(x,2) column or a Decimal.toFixed(2), so >2dp never occurs; tightening to throw risks rejecting a currently-working edge. Noted.
- Non-cumulative cap path (Money.multiplyRate), roundDivide HALF_UP, priorAmounts ASC ordering, yearsSinceBase = priors+1 all re-verified penny-exact vs oracle.

### Finder C: accepted CLEAN (0 bugs) from prior triage.

**Status:** Cycle 48 shipped 1 fail-closed GL money-fidelity pattern-align (the only unambiguous defect); surfaced 3 tasks (#60/#61 import re-upload idempotency = decision-gated schema/UX; #62 cap base_year history filter = needs CAM research). 2 HIGH/MED parser findings ruled FALSE POSITIVE (negatives rejected by design in the billing importer, different contract from the GL parser). DURABLE LESSONS: (a) **the "lone-outlier sibling" pattern cuts both ways.** A money column read uncast while 5 siblings cast it IS a real fail-closed pattern-align worth shipping (GL amount::text). But a parser missing its sibling's hardening is NOT automatically a bug, read the FULL consumer path first: the billing importer's `amount.lte(0)` reject-negatives design means every U+2212/CR/paren-CR format the finder cited drops either way, so mirroring the GL parser changes nothing financial. Contracts differ (GL accepts signed reversals; billed amounts are positive-only). (b) two independent finders converging on the same site is strong evidence of PRESENCE but not of SEVERITY, both over-labeled the GL cast CRITICAL/HIGH; the honest impact is LOW (porsager numeric round-trips for realistic money), the ship justification is pattern-consistency + fail-closed, not corrupted-totals. (c) re-upload/re-import idempotency (actual-billed, rent-roll) is a recurring decision-gated class, the fix always touches schema (no dedup key) + UX (replace vs version vs reject) + preservation of downstream manual edits; surface as a task, never autonomously add a unique constraint. (d) an oracle/Worker DIVERGENCE is not auto-a-Worker-bug, when the financially-correct behavior is genuinely unclear (cap bank base_year filtering), it needs CAM research + product intent, not a reflexive port to match the oracle.

### SHIPPED: cap-bank `tenant_share_before_cap` NUMERIC read ::text-cast (master ad4ab53e9; capveri-api 100% 4b570997, /health healthy)

Finder A's exhaustive sweep of every `adapters/db/*.ts` SELECT found 4 uncast-NUMERIC candidates, ALL in `reconciliation.ts`. The decisive adversarial split is **internal-consumer (Decimal/String→Decimal, zero-observable) vs outward-facing (serialized directly to a `c.json` HTTP response, where the cast flips the wire type number→string or normalizes trailing zeros, an observable API-contract change, NOT zero-behavior)**, cross-checked against the DECLARED TYPES (domain/reconciliation/repository.ts:51-89):
- Money columns are typed `string | number | null`, the union **deliberately admits** porsager's runtime float (the codebase's explicit acknowledgment that these ship the driver number). So they are NOT a contract violation; the type tells the truth. Contrast the date columns, typed pure `string`, that's why the C25 getSnapshot date-coercion shipped (a runtime Date violated the declared `string` AND crashed an internal `.slice()` in reconciliationUrl). Money has neither property.
- Severity: NUMERIC(14,2) (≤14 sig digits) round-trips EXACTLY through JS shortest-round-trip (`String()`, `JSON.stringify`, `new Decimal(number)` all reproduce the exact 2dp string) → there is NO numeric corruption on ANY path. The finder's "1234.5600000000001" precision-loss story is wrong. The only real difference a cast makes is the string FORM (trailing zeros: "1000" vs "1000.00") and JSON type (number vs string).

**Candidate rulings:**
1. `snapshotSummarySelect`/`listSnapshots` (:87-102, :530): total_recovery/tenant_share_after_cap/admin_fee returned **directly via c.json to the HTTP client**. Cast flips wire type number→string. **By-design / outward-facing, NOT shipped.** The `string|number` union is deliberate; not a correctness bug.
2. `getSnapshot select *` (:503) → normalizeSnapshotJsonFields (:1494) coerces DATES to strings but not money → money emitted to **c.json as JSON numbers**. Same outward-facing flip. **By-design, NOT shipped.** (The date coercion was justified by pure-string type + internal `.slice()` crash; money has neither.)
3. **cap-bank `tenant_share_before_cap` (:1088)** → consumed at cap-bank-ledger.ts:248-250 `String(s.tenant_share_before_cap ?? "0")` → `simulateCapBank` (**INTERNAL**, parsed by decimal.js). "1000"/"1000.00"/float-String all parse to the identical Decimal → **zero observable change end-to-end**. ### SHIPPED - cross-doc review status cannot regress from `reviewed` to `in_review`

Finder Jason found a stale-status race in `PATCH /cross-doc-analysis/:analysisId/findings/:findingId`:

- Finding-decision JSONB merge is atomic and org-scoped.
- Status advancement then re-reads analysis status/findings.
- If request A reads `pending` and partial decisions, request B can complete all decisions and set `reviewed`, then request A can resume and write `in_review`.
- The old repository `updateAnalysisStatus` only scoped by `id` and `organization_id`, so a stale partial reviewer could overwrite terminal `reviewed`.

Fix:
- `CrossDocAnalysisRepository.updateAnalysisStatus` now returns `boolean` and accepts optional `expectedStatus`.
- The Postgres adapter adds an optional `and status = $4` predicate plus `returning id`.
- Only `pending -> in_review` passes `expectedStatus: "pending"`.
- `reviewed` transitions stay unguarded so the all-findings-decided request can still close from either `pending` or `in_review`.

## Cycle 65 - redelivered reconciliation running jobs fail recoverably; state-machine/provenance backlog refined

**3 parallel read-only finders pinned to the deployed TypeScript Worker. Net: 1 fail-closed queue recovery fix shipped; several fresh optimistic-concurrency and source-evidence slices queued for the next cycle or decision-gated.**

### SHIPPED - redelivered running reconciliation jobs no longer silently ack

Finder Bacon found a real queue recovery gap in the reconciliation workflow:

- `POST /api/v1/reconciliation/calculate` creates a `pending` calculation job and enqueues `{ version, jobId, organizationId }`.
- The queue runner claims work with `pending -> running`.
- If the Worker isolate dies after claim and before the catch block marks the job failed, Cloudflare redelivers the message.
- The old workflow returned for any non-`pending` job, so a redelivered message for a still-`running` job would return normally and be acked, leaving the job permanently stuck.

Fix:

- `createReconciliationQueueHandlers` now passes the raw queue message into the runner.
- The runner preserves existing pending-job behavior.
- On redelivery (`attempts > 1`) where the DB job is still `running`, it calls a new guarded repository method and returns normally so the redelivered queue message can ack after the job is made retryable by user action.
- `PostgresReconciliationRepository.markRunningCalculationFailed` updates only `status = 'running'` rows for the same org/job and returns whether the guarded transition matched. It does not use the existing unguarded `markCalculationFailed`, avoiding a race with late successful completion.
- Redelivered `completed` and `failed` jobs remain no-op.

## Cycle 68 - Stripe paid invoice state cannot be reopened by stale webhooks

**Launched 3 fresh read-only Worker-pinned finders. Net: 1 fail-closed Stripe webhook state guard shipped, 1 artifact mismatch recorded for future triage, 1 security sweep clean.**

### SHIPPED - paid invoices cannot regress to open/non-paid on out-of-order webhooks

Finder Faraday found that Stripe invoice events can arrive out of order. `invoice.paid` could mark an invoice `paid`, then a delayed `invoice.created` conflict update or delayed `invoice.payment_failed` could overwrite the same `stripe_invoice_id` back to `open`/non-paid. Duplicate event claiming did not prevent this because different Stripe event ids for the same invoice process independently.

Fix:

- `PostgresStripeWebhookRepository.upsertInvoice` now keeps existing paid invoices intact on the `on conflict (stripe_invoice_id)` update path.
- `PostgresStripeWebhookRepository.markInvoiceOpen` now refuses to reopen rows whose current status is `paid`.
- `markInvoicePaid` is unchanged, so `invoice.paid` can still create/match a missing invoice and mark it paid.
- No invoice schema migration was introduced; broader event timestamp ordering remains out of scope for this narrow paid-state guard.

## Cycle 71 - extraction queue processing claim is exclusive and retry-safe

Cycle 71 launched three fresh Worker-pinned read-only finder sweeps:

- Gibbs audited export/download signed-token and public file surfaces. Result: CLEAN for shippable IDOR/scope/R2-prefix defects. Historical PDF public HMAC links remain policy-gated because 7-day links have no export-history row for revocation.
- Maxwell audited async/webhook idempotency. Found the shipped extraction queue processing-claim bug. Resend inbound webhook forwarding without a persisted Svix event ledger remains decision-gated. Stripe/reconciliation paths were clean.
- Pascal audited low-traffic state machines. Found decision-gated auth lifecycle account-deletion race semantics and feedback terminal-status/metadata semantics. Cross-doc, property import, actual-billed, and onboard upgrade were clean/by-design.

### SHIPPED - extraction queue redeliveries no longer rerun processing jobs or lose early retries

`processExtractionQueueMessage` now atomically claims extraction jobs before running the pipeline and treats claim misses according to the observed job state.

Fix:

- `ExtractionJobRepository.markProcessing(jobId, expectedStatus)` now returns `boolean`.
- The Postgres adapter updates to `processing` only when the row is currently `pending`, or currently `retrying` with `next_retry_at <= now()`, and uses `returning id` to prove the claim succeeded.
- Processing redeliveries that lose the claim return without rerunning the extraction pipeline.
- Retry deliveries that arrive before `next_retry_at`, or retrying rows with null/invalid retry timestamps, throw `ExtractionRetryScheduledError`, so the queue consumer calls `retry({ delaySeconds })` instead of `ack()`.
- The repository now loads `next_retry_at` so the service can preserve the remaining retry delay for early retry deliveries.
- No schema migration was introduced.

### Durable lesson

Queue claim misses are not all idempotent no-ops. A claim miss for an already-processing job should not rerun the pipeline, but a claim miss for a retrying job can represent "not due yet" and must keep the queue message alive. Make the repository claim predicate fail-closed, then route service-level misses by observed status so due-time jitter does not strand recoverable jobs.

### SHIPPED - CapEx bulk review is all-or-none

`POST /api/v1/analysis/capex-flags/bulk-review` no longer validates IDs first and then reviews each flag through independent updates. That old read-validate-write split could partially review earlier flags and then return `404` if a later flag disappeared or moved org after pre-validation.

Fix:

- Added `CapExRepository.reviewFlags`.
- `PostgresCapExRepository.reviewFlags` runs in one transaction.
- It locks all unique requested flag rows with `for update`.
- If any requested ID is missing or belongs to another org, it returns `not_found` before any update runs.
- Otherwise it updates all locked flags in one statement and expands the response back to the original request order, including duplicate request IDs.
- The single-flag review route remains unchanged.
- No schema migration was introduced.

If the route promises all-or-none behavior, put the validation and mutation in one repository transaction and make the missing-row path return before any update statement runs. Preserve request-order response shape separately from the database update shape so duplicate IDs do not force repeated writes.

## Cycle 78 - reconciliation persistence finalized-race guard

Cycle 78 launched three fresh Worker-pinned read-only finder sweeps from clean `origin/master` head `74d641f7f`. Pasteur found billing/export state machines clean except known gated policy items. Meitner found the shipped reconciliation persistence finalized-race guard. Epicurus found tenant/dispute/notification/admin lifecycle surfaces clean except known gated policy items.

### SHIPPED - reconciliation result persistence rechecks finalized periods under lock

The workflow checked for finalized snapshots before loading data and computing reconciliation results. But `persistCalculationResults()` later deleted draft snapshots, inserted new draft snapshots, and completed the job in a transaction without taking the property financial-evidence advisory lock or re-checking finalized snapshots inside that same transaction.

Race fixed: a queued `force_recalculate` job could pass the pre-compute finalized check, another request could finalize the same property/period under `lockPropertyFinancialEvidence`, then the queued job could persist new draft snapshots after a finalized period already existed.

Fix: `persistCalculationResults()` now calls `lockPropertyFinancialEvidence()` at the start of its transaction, then re-runs `hasFinalizedSnapshotForPeriod()` inside the locked transaction before draft delete/insert/complete. If a finalized snapshot exists, it throws the existing immutable-period message so the workflow marks the job failed through the existing catch path. No schema or route contract change.

Ship: fix commit `8f7b02171`; merge commit `955a66525`; pushed `master` to `origin/master`; deployed `capveri-api` version `7bfcc6cf-5bf7-4404-8c1e-5cd3c37eddde`; Cloudflare deployment status showed `(100%) 7bfcc6cf-5bf7-4404-8c1e-5cd3c37eddde`; `curl.exe -i https://api.capveri.com/health` returned `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`.

Verification: branch focused reconciliation tests 2 files/33 passed; branch typecheck pass; branch lint pass; branch full backend `npm test` 121 files/1901 passed/12 skipped; code review clean/ready with lock/finalized-check parameter assertions added; rebased branch repeated focused/typecheck/lint/full all green; merged-head repeated focused/typecheck/lint/full all green. Local reconciliation E2E was attempted and failed with expected `1992.02`, got `2267.12`; the identical failure reproduced on clean `origin/master`, so this is pre-existing local harness/data drift, not caused by the patch.

Decision-gated / clean notes: billing/export state machines clean; tenant/dispute/notification lifecycle surfaces clean; actual-billed finalized mutation guards already lock then check finalized overlap; document approve/delete finalized lease-reference guards already lock before checking. Decision-gated backlog remains: `#56`, `#60`, `#61`, `C73-L1`, `C65-S1`, `C63-P1`, `#65`, `C74-B1`, `C72-E2`, `C62-G1`, `C62-G2`, `#52`, `#48`, and related source-evidence/versioning policies.

Durable lesson: pre-compute immutability checks are not enough when calculation can take time. Any queue workflow that computes outside the write transaction must re-acquire the same domain lock and re-check terminal/finalized state immediately before persistence.

## Cycle 79 - extraction queue org scoping and public export download headers

Cycle 79 launched three fresh Worker-pinned read-only finder sweeps from clean `origin/master` head `955a66525`. Newton found the shipped extraction queue cross-org mutation bug. Ramanujan found the shipped public signed export download header gap. Curie found broader artifact hardening backlog items around PDF Unicode text and header-safe filenames.

### SHIPPED - extraction queue cannot fail or process another org's job/document from a stale/wrong-org message

`processExtractionQueueMessage()` previously loaded a job by id, then fell back by document id, without scoping those loads to the queued organization. If the loaded job/document context mismatched, it marked that loaded job and document failed and returned, causing the poison message to be acked after cross-org mutation.

Fix: extraction job lookups now require `organizationId`; SQL filters `jobs.organization_id` and requires the joined document to share the job organization; `markJobAndDocumentFailed()` now scopes both `extraction_jobs` and `documents` updates by organization; context mismatches return without mutation.

### SHIPPED - public signed export downloads send private/no-sniff headers

`GET /api/v1/export/download/file` now returns `Cache-Control: private, max-age=0, no-store` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. The local exports E2E now asserts those headers on public XLSX re-download and corrects a stale expectation to the existing spreadsheet MIME route behavior.

Ship: fix commit `15f0093d9`; merge commit `951e2c8ac`; pushed `master` to `origin/master`; deployed `capveri-api` version `e89ceb11-5d8e-4c0a-a171-934c79f36656`; Cloudflare deployment status showed `(100%) e89ceb11-5d8e-4c0a-a171-934c79f36656`; `curl.exe -i https://api.capveri.com/health` returned `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`.

Verification: branch focused tests 3 files/135 passed; branch typecheck pass; branch lint pass; branch full backend `npm test` 121 files/1902 passed/12 skipped; branch local exports E2E `ok: true`; code review found a P2 join-level org-scope gap, fixed, and follow-up review returned no findings. Merged-head focused tests 3 files/135 passed; merged-head typecheck pass; merged-head lint pass; merged-head full backend `npm test` 121 files/1902 passed/12 skipped; merged-head local exports E2E `ok: true`.

Decision-gated / backlog notes: PDF Unicode text and centralized header-safe filename handling are real artifact hardening items but broader than this zero-policy-change patch. Existing decision-gated backlog remains unchanged.

Durable lesson: tenant scoping on a queue lookup is not complete if the selected row joins to another tenant-owned row. For queue consumers that bypass request-time RLS, scope the requested entity, scope the joined evidence row, and scope terminal writes. Poison/stale messages should be acked without mutating rows when they cannot become valid.

## Cycle 80 - reconciliation redelivery guard, header-safe downloads, SB1103 export cache

Cycle 80 launched three fresh read-only finder sweeps from clean `origin/master` head `951e2c8ac`, then integrated over current `origin/master` head `d508ac09d`. Plato found the shipped reconciliation queue stale-completion race. Hilbert found the shipped property-derived filename header-safety gaps. Schrodinger found the shipped SB1103 export cache invalidation gap.

### SHIPPED - reconciliation result persistence refuses stale completions

If Cloudflare redelivered a reconciliation message while the first worker was still computing, the redelivery path could mark the `running` job failed. The original worker still held its in-memory job and later called `persistCalculationResults()`, which inserted snapshots and completed the job without rechecking job state.

Fix: `persistCalculationResults()` now locks and verifies the calculation job is still `running` before financial-evidence lock, finalized-period recheck, draft deletion, snapshot insertion, or job completion. `completeCalculationJobRow()` updates only `status = 'running'` and throws if no row matched. Repository tests prove stale/non-running jobs abort before snapshot mutation.

### SHIPPED - property-derived download filenames are header-safe

Added a shared attachment filename helper that strips C0 controls/DEL and replaces quotes. Applied to tenant statement PDFs, tenant/admin dispute attachments, public export token downloads, and tax protest ZIPs.

### SHIPPED - SB1103 export invalidates the request list

`useExportSB1103Request()` now invalidates the full SB1103 query namespace after successful export, so the list refetches `status`, `export_format`, and `exported_at` after the backend marks a request exported.

Ship: fix commit `f6c9d6d4e`; merge commit `5f9d9a1bc`; pushed `master` to `origin/master`; deployed `capveri-api` version `9f150466-c794-4778-acdf-b2827ec1d24c`; `capveri-api` deployment status showed `(100%) 9f150466-c794-4778-acdf-b2827ec1d24c`; `curl.exe -i https://api.capveri.com/health` returned `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`; deployed `capveri-app` version `2c0976fb-758a-4437-a0f0-a7ad5b33b48e`; `capveri-app` deployment status showed `(100%) 2c0976fb-758a-4437-a0f0-a7ad5b33b48e`; `curl.exe -I https://app.capveri.com/` returned `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`.

Verification: branch and merged-head backend focused tests 6 files/231 passed; backend typecheck pass; backend lint pass; backend full `npm test` 121 files/1905 passed/12 skipped; backend local E2Es exports/tax-protest/tenant-portal-disputes all `ok: true`; frontend typecheck pass; frontend lint pass; focused SB1103 hooks test 1 file/3 passed; code review no findings.

Known unrelated failures: frontend full `npx vitest run` failed only two `PropertyFormPage` cancel tests expecting `navigate(-1)` while current app calls `navigate('/properties')`; the same two failures reproduced on a clean `origin/master` baseline worktree. Local reconciliation E2E still fails with the known pre-existing total drift expected `1992.02`, got `2267.12`.

Durable lesson: atomic result persistence must prove both domain immutability and job ownership/state at the moment of write. A queue redelivery can legitimately fail a still-running job; the original worker must not later complete from stale memory. Lock the job row and require the expected state before inserting any derived results.
